clips.text_zh: Bull run starts tonight. Lots of Bitcoin options expire today at 4pm EST. 今日係關鍵位，睇下成個market點反應啦。
clips.text_en_b1: A bull run starts tonight, according to the original poster. Lots of Bitcoin options expire today at 4pm EST. Traders are watching whether that expiry will trigger a strong move in the market tonight.
clips.text_en_b2: According to the original poster, the Bitcoin bull run could start tonight, although a lot of options are expiring today at 4pm EST. This expiry may be a crucial turning point for the market, so traders are keeping a close eye on how prices react. Although one session of options expiring does not guarantee a sustained rally, the concentration of expiring contracts could still trigger significant volatility and a strong move tonight.
clips.text_en_c1: According to the original poster, a Bitcoin bull run could begin tonight, although the timing remains uncertain. A substantial number of Bitcoin options are due to expire today at 4 p.m. EST, making the session a potentially pivotal test of market sentiment. Traders are closely monitoring whether the expiry will provide enough liquidity or momentum to trigger a sharp move in either direction. If the resulting reaction gains strength, it could establish the short-term trend; if not, traders may be left facing another period of consolidation.
clips.text_en_c2: According to the original poster, the bull run begins tonight, with an unusually large concentration of Bitcoin options expiring at 4 p.m. EST. Although expiry does not mechanically dictate direction, it can amplify volatility as traders adjust or close positions and market makers rebalance exposure. The poster regards today’s expiry as the decisive session, suggesting that its effects may determine whether Bitcoin stages a strong move tonight. With so much contract value concentrated around one deadline, even seemingly routine hedging flows could send the market sharply higher or expose its fragile side.
clips.source_hint: The poster expects a Bitcoin bull run around today's options expiry.

clips.text_zh: CZ 同 Elon 之間搞到成個public brodown。Elon 笑咗Binance今日嘅hack，睇下crypto market會唔會再震一震。
clips.text_en_b1: It is going down between CZ and Elon, and the poster says this is not a drill. They are having a total public breakdown after Elon went and laughed at Binance for today’s hack. The post is focused on the possible impact on crypto sentiment.
clips.text_en_b2: The poster insists that the public clash between CZ and Elon Musk is going down, adding that this is definitely not a drill. Their disagreement has developed into a full-scale online breakdown after Elon laughed at Binance over its hack today. Although the argument may appear entertaining, the post is mainly concerned about how negative headlines could affect crypto sentiment, particularly if the exchange’s problems remain in the headlines.
clips.text_en_c1: The disagreement between CZ and Elon Musk has escalated into what the poster describes as a full-scale public breakdown, adding to an already volatile week. Musk responded to Binance’s latest hack by laughing at the exchange, a move that CZ appears to have taken personally. What began as a clash between two prominent figures may now spill over into the wider crypto community. The immediate concern is whether the exchange of insults damages confidence in Binance and, by extension, weighs on broader crypto sentiment.
clips.text_en_c2: The dispute between CZ and Elon Musk has, in the poster’s words, escalated into a very public breakdown rather than a routine disagreement. Musk’s ridicule of Binance following the exchange’s hack on the day provided the flashpoint. The post is less concerned with the technical details of the breach than with the reputational damage inflicted on Binance and the wider crypto market. If sentiment is already brittle, a high-profile humiliation from Musk could provoke another round of fear, selling pressure, and volatility, leaving traders to consider whether the crypto market is heading for another turbulent night.
clips.source_hint: The post links the CZ-Elon dispute and Binance hack to crypto-market drama.

clips.text_zh: Compute 先係最值得invest嘅嘢。無論係stocks定真實chips，Nvidia、semis嗰啲先係核心。Neocloud只係reseller，無自己product同software就更加唔穩陣。AI咁勁，優化business嘅同時，隨時直接抹殺原本個business，靠AI續命都未必救到。
clips.text_en_b1: Compute is the only thing you should invest in, whether that means stocks or physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are mentioned directly. Neoclouds are just resellers without their own products, while software is risky because AI might eat it.
clips.text_en_b2: The argument is that compute is the only area worth investing in, whether through semiconductor stocks or actual chips, with Nvidia and the broader chip industry at the core. Neoclouds are dismissed as resellers because they lack their own hardware and software. Although AI can improve business efficiency, it may also wipe out existing products outright, so companies relying on AI to extend their lifespan should not assume they will be safe.
clips.text_en_c1: The poster argues that compute is the only asset worth investing in, whether one buys semiconductor stocks or physical chips, with Nvidia and the broader chip industry occupying the centre of the thesis. Neoclouds, by contrast, are dismissed as resellers that lack proprietary products and software, making their position inherently fragile. Software is also treated as a risky proposition because rapidly advancing AI may absorb business models that once appeared defensible. In such cases, companies relying on AI to extend a declining operation may not survive the transition.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster’s central thesis is that investors should concentrate on compute, whether they express that conviction through semiconductor stocks or the physical chips themselves. Nvidia and the broader semiconductor industry are therefore identified as the genuine core of the opportunity, rather than businesses that merely rent access to that infrastructure. Neoclouds, in this view, are resellers without proprietary products or software, making their position inherently less defensible. Software is arguably riskier still, since rapidly advancing AI may not merely improve existing businesses but quietly eliminate them outright, leaving even companies that rely on AI to prolong their relevance without any guarantee of survival.
clips.source_hint: The poster argues that compute and semiconductors are better investments than software businesses.

clips.text_zh: Proton個CEO向engineering department發AI manifesto，仲用一種幾离谱嘅語氣問：點解大家成日用LLM，productivity反而冇升？係咪佢食錯AI psychosis pills？
clips.text_en_b1: Proton’s CEO sent an AI manifesto to the engineering department. He asked employees why their productivity had not increased, even though they were using the LLM all the time. The poster questions whether he is right or suffering from AI psychosis.
clips.text_en_b2: Proton’s CEO recently sent an AI manifesto to the engineering department, apparently in an unusually blunt tone. He questioned why employees had not become more productive despite using an LLM all the time. The poster wonders whether the CEO has identified a genuine problem with workplace AI adoption or whether he is simply suffering from what they call “AI psychosis.” Either way, the memo has sparked some uncomfortable questions about productivity.
clips.text_en_c1: Proton’s CEO has circulated an AI manifesto within the engineering department, prompting the poster to question whether its author has lost touch with reality. In an unusual and rather extreme tone, the CEO asks employees why their productivity has not increased despite using large language models constantly. Rather than treating adoption as a straightforward success, the message suggests that greater reliance on AI has failed to deliver the expected gains. The poster then wonders whether the CEO’s diagnosis is entirely wrong or whether he is suffering from what they call “AI psychosis.”
clips.text_en_c2: Proton’s CEO circulated an AI manifesto throughout the engineering department, adopting an almost absurdly confrontational tone in the process. His central question was why employees’ productivity had failed to rise despite their constant use of large language models. The irony is difficult to miss: an executive seeking to extract measurable gains from AI appears to have received productivity that failed to materialise, and instead responded with pointed internal criticism. The original poster captures the joke by asking whether the CEO has landed on a useful insight or whether, rather more dramatically, he is suffering from what the post calls ‘AI psychosis.’
clips.source_hint: The post questions Proton’s CEO after his unusual AI-productivity memo.

clips.text_zh: 點解美國好似唔會invest高-speed rail？但歐洲同中國都做得。講真，American infrastructure成日係plan一大撈，落地又慢。
clips.text_en_b1: Why doesn’t the US invest in high-speed rail like Europe and China? The question points to a visible infrastructure gap between the United States and countries with extensive high-speed rail networks.
clips.text_en_b2: The post asks why the United States seems unwilling to invest in high-speed rail, even though Europe and China have built extensive networks. It suggests that this reflects a wider weakness in American infrastructure: grand plans are often announced, but implementation takes far too long. Although the comparison highlights a visible gap between the US and other countries, it also raises questions about funding, political priorities, and whether large projects can ever be completed efficiently.
clips.text_en_c1: The poster asks why the United States appears so unlikely to invest seriously in high-speed rail, even though Europe and China have built extensive networks capable of transforming domestic travel. This highlights a striking infrastructure gap between America and its major economic counterparts. In the poster’s view, American infrastructure policy is too often dominated by ambitious planning, lengthy approval processes and delays between announcement and execution. Unless political priorities and funding arrangements change, the country is likely to continue underinvesting in rail systems that other developed and emerging economies treat as essential.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster asks why the United States appears so reluctant to invest in high-speed rail when both Europe and China have built extensive networks capable of connecting major cities at speed. This is not merely a transport question; it exposes a conspicuous infrastructure deficit and, arguably, a broader failure of long-term planning. American infrastructure projects are frequently criticised for grand announcements, lengthy approval processes, spiralling costs, and painfully slow construction once funding supposedly becomes available. Meanwhile, comparable systems abroad are already operational, suggesting that political fragmentation and institutional inertia have left the United States watching rivals build the infrastructure of the future.
clips.source_hint: The thread asks why the United States has not developed European and Chinese-style high-speed rail.

clips.text_zh: Barbell Hack Squat：lower back strain比squat同deadlift少，bar又近center of mass，load可以重啲。唔使rack，fail都容易bail；form散就bar會撞hamstring。
clips.text_en_b1: Barbell Hack Squat claims zero lower-back strain compared with squats or deadlifts. The bar stays closer to the center of mass, potentially allowing heavier loads. It needs no rack, is easy to bail from, and checks form when the bar hits the hamstrings.
clips.text_en_b2: The Barbell Hack Squat is presented as a safer alternative to squats and deadlifts because it reportedly places much less strain on the lower back. Since the bar stays closer to the center of mass, lifters may be able to handle heavier loads. It also requires no rack and is easy to bail from if a set goes wrong. However, poor form can cause the bar to strike the hamstrings, so technique still matters.
clips.text_en_c1: The Barbell Hack Squat is presented as a lower-back-friendly alternative to squats and deadlifts, although “zero strain” should be understood as the poster’s strong claim rather than an absolute guarantee. Because the bar remains relatively close to the centre of mass, lifters may be able to handle heavier loads than they would in comparable exercises. The movement also requires no rack and allows a failed rep to be abandoned more easily. Form still matters: if the position deteriorates, the bar can travel down into the hamstrings, making the exercise unforgiving of poor technique.
clips.text_en_c2: The barbell hack squat is presented as a lower-stress alternative to conventional squats and deadlifts, with less strain on the lower back because the bar remains comparatively close to the body’s centre of mass. That positioning may make it possible to handle heavier loads while reducing the demand on the spine. Another practical advantage is that no rack is required, and a lifter can bail out relatively easily if the movement deteriorates. The exercise nevertheless has a useful built-in check on technique: when the bar collides with the hamstrings, the lifter’s position has almost certainly broken down, signalling the need to reset rather than continue.
clips.source_hint: The post lists the supposed benefits of using a barbell hack squat.

clips.text_zh: 最近Shonen Jump係咪個股勁？新story對海外同日本讀者都好似好boring。Oda可能係唯一仲撐住個magazine嘅人。不過核心audience而家都30歲，個市場同讀者都老咗。
clips.text_en_b1: Let’s discuss the recent issues of Shonen Jump. Every new story seems boring to overseas and Japanese readers. The poster says Oda is the only thing keeping the magazine relevant, while its core audience is now around 30 years old.
clips.text_en_b2: The discussion focuses on recent issues of Shonen Jump, with the poster claiming that every new story seems boring to both overseas and Japanese readers. Oda may be the only major creator still holding the magazine together, although his popularity alone may not solve its deeper problems. The core audience is now around 30 years old, suggesting that the market has aged along with its readers, creating a challenge for attracting younger fans.
clips.text_en_c1: Recent issues of Shonen Jump have struck the poster as exceptionally uninspired, with the newest stories appearing equally unappealing to overseas readers and to audiences in Japan itself. The discussion portrays Oda as the principal figure still capable of keeping the magazine relevant, suggesting that without his established appeal, its broader reputation would weaken considerably. At the same time, the publication’s core readership is now around thirty years old. This ageing audience, combined with changing tastes and an increasingly competitive market, has left the magazine facing a serious challenge.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster invites discussion of Shonen Jump’s recent issues, on the grounds that every new story appears tedious to both overseas and Japanese readers. The criticism is not confined to individual series; it suggests that the magazine may have lost whatever energy once made it compelling to its domestic audience. Eiichiro Oda is identified as the principal figure still holding the publication together, perhaps providing the audience and commercial visibility that lesser-known works no longer command. Yet the underlying problem is demographic: the core readership is now around thirty years old, meaning that both the magazine and the market it serves are ageing together.
clips.source_hint: The poster complains about recent Shonen Jump stories and says Oda is carrying the magazine.

clips.text_zh: AI 對 Bitcoin 有冇威脅？我如果係你，依家就買 Gold。靠，Bitcoin 同 gold 擺埋一齊睇，AI 呢股氣真係越吹越恐怖。Golden。
clips.text_en_b1: Have you followed the developments in AI and the threat it poses to Bitcoin? I would buy gold now if I were you. AI is getting stronger, and Bitcoin may face a bigger challenge ahead. This post clearly favors gold over Bitcoin right now.
clips.text_en_b2: Have you followed the rapid developments in artificial intelligence and the threat it poses to Bitcoin? If I were you, I would buy gold now. When you place Bitcoin and gold side by side, the momentum behind AI looks increasingly frightening. AI is becoming stronger, so Bitcoin may be headed for a much bigger challenge ahead. Although this remains an opinion, the post clearly favors gold over Bitcoin at the moment.
clips.text_en_c1: Have you followed the latest developments in artificial intelligence and the threat they pose to Bitcoin? If I were you, I would buy gold now. Set Bitcoin and gold side by side, and the momentum behind AI is becoming increasingly alarming. As AI continues to improve, Bitcoin may face a considerably bigger challenge ahead, whereas gold appears to be the safer option. The post clearly favours gold over Bitcoin at this particular moment, although that does not make the recommendation a guarantee of future performance.
clips.text_en_c2: Have you been following recent advances in artificial intelligence and the mounting threat they pose to Bitcoin? If I were you, I would buy gold now, because placing Bitcoin and gold side by side makes the AI narrative increasingly difficult to ignore. As the technology continues to strengthen, Bitcoin may be facing a considerably more serious challenge ahead of it. Although the precise impact remains uncertain, the prevailing mood is unmistakably bullish toward gold. The post therefore signals a clear preference for traditional precious metals over Bitcoin at present, however speculative such a comparison may ultimately prove.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post says AI threatens Bitcoin and recommends buying gold.

clips.text_zh: Compute 先係你唯一應該投資嘅嘢。股票又好，真實晶片又好。Semi、Nvidia 都得。Neocloud 只係轉售商，自己冇 product 同 software。AI 可能食晒 software，連 hyperscaler 都未必安全。Google 試過 implement AI，反而 killing 自己 search ad business。科技太猛，優化 business 途中可能直接 wipe it out。靠，今個年代仲要靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: Compute is the only thing you should invest in, whether that means stocks or physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the main ideas. Neoclouds are only resellers without their own products, while software is risky because AI may eat it. Even hyperscalers face trouble: Google is damaging its search ad business while implementing AI.
clips.text_en_b2: Compute is the only thing you should invest in, whether that means buying shares or physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the main ideas, whereas neoclouds are merely resellers with neither their own products nor their own software. Software is risky because AI may swallow whole categories of businesses. Even hyperscalers are not safe, as Google is damaging its search advertising business while implementing AI. Technology is advancing so quickly that optimisation can wipe out the original business.
clips.text_en_c1: Compute is the only asset I would seriously consider investing in, whether that means buying shares in semiconductor companies or acquiring physical chips. The main ideas are semis and Nvidia. Neoclouds, by contrast, are merely resellers with neither their own products nor their own software, which makes them considerably less compelling. Software is also risky because AI may gradually absorb many of its functions. Even hyperscalers are not immune: Google, for example, appears to be damaging its search advertising business while implementing AI. In such a rapidly evolving industry, optimisation can end up wiping out the very business it is meant to strengthen.
clips.text_en_c2: Compute is the one asset class you should seriously consider investing in, whether through equities or ownership of physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the principal ideas, whereas neoclouds appear to function merely as resellers, with neither proprietary products nor distinctive software of their own. Software itself is precarious, since AI may absorb much of the value it currently creates. Even hyperscalers are not immune: Google has been implementing AI while undermining its own search-advertising business. In technology, optimisation can be so disruptive that it wipes out the very business it is intended to strengthen.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post argues that compute, chips, and semiconductors are the strongest investment theme.

clips.text_zh: 有人話 load path 只係背書，講完就算。但我哋做 structural work，最怕 load path 講唔清。Beam 接到 column，column 落到 foundation，force 點樣傳，點解嗰個 member 咁做，全部都要 check。靠AI續命都要自己識睇图，唔可以只靠 AI 砌故事。
clips.text_en_b1: Understand how loads travel through a structure. Loads move through beams, columns, connections, and foundations. A civil engineer must explain why each member exists and how it was checked. This basic knowledge helps when reviewing drawings and discussing work with contractors on site.
clips.text_en_b2: Some people treat load paths as nothing more than jargon to memorise before moving on. However, structural work becomes dangerous when nobody can explain how forces actually travel. You need to know how a beam connects to a column, how the column transfers its load into the foundation, and why each member has been designed in that particular way. AI may keep us employed, but engineers still need to read drawings and build sound judgements rather than simply asking it to invent convincing stories.
clips.text_en_c1: Some people treat load paths as little more than paperwork: identify the system, draw an arrow, and move on. Yet anyone doing structural work knows that failing to explain how forces travel can be dangerous. Loads pass from beams into columns, through connections, and ultimately into foundations, so every member must be justified. When reviewing drawings or discussing structural decisions with contractors on site, it is essential to understand why each component exists and how it has been checked. AI may help engineers keep pace, but it cannot replace the judgement required to read drawings rather than merely generate plausible-sounding stories.
clips.text_en_c2: Some dismiss load-path analysis as little more than rote theory: explain the principle, tick the box, and move on. Yet anyone engaged in structural work knows that an incomprehensible load path is a source of profound anxiety. How does a beam transfer force into a column? How does that column carry the load into the foundation? Why is each member proportioned and arranged as it is? Every aspect must be checked. AI may keep us employed, but it cannot substitute for the ability to read drawings critically and interrogate the underlying engineering story.
clips.source_hint: The gaming thread describes growing overwhelmed as quests become more complicated.

clips.text_zh: Future is coming at you, anons。Claude 依家已經開始做 brain surgery，仲係其中一個 hardest fields。靠AI續命真係唔係講笑。AI 可能先食 blue collar，再食 white collar。Professional exam 都未考完，唔可以淨係靠 AI 幫我讀書。
clips.text_en_b1: The future is coming at us, anons. Claude is now doing brain surgery, one of the hardest fields for anyone to master. This development shows how quickly AI is moving into serious professional work. However, AI cannot replace the knowledge needed for engineering exams and site decisions.
clips.text_en_b2: The future is coming at us, anons, and Claude has already begun performing brain surgery, which is among the hardest fields anyone can master. Clearly, this is no longer some distant prospect, so relying on AI to keep us employed is hardly a joke. AI may first replace blue-collar work and then move into white-collar professions. Even so, it cannot supply the underlying knowledge required to pass professional engineering exams or make sound decisions on site.
clips.text_en_c1: The future is coming at us, anons, and Claude is already being used in brain surgery, one of the most demanding fields anyone can master. That development demonstrates how quickly AI is moving into serious professional work, rather than merely handling routine office tasks. AI may first displace blue-collar roles and then move into white-collar professions, although this does not mean expertise has become irrelevant. If you have not even finished your professional examinations, you cannot rely on AI to complete your education for you. It may assist with learning, but the underlying knowledge required for engineering exams and on-site decisions still has to be yours.
clips.text_en_c2: The future is bearing down on us, anons. Claude is already being used in brain surgery, one of the most exacting and difficult fields any professional must master. This is not a trivial application or a convenient thought experiment; it illustrates how rapidly AI is advancing into work where mistakes may have irreversible consequences. The broader implication is equally unsettling: AI may first displace blue-collar work and subsequently erode many white-collar professions. Nevertheless, no system can replace the foundational knowledge required to pass professional examinations, exercise sound judgement on site, and recognise when an automated recommendation should not be trusted.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ post says Claude is now performing brain surgery.

clips.text_zh: Tesla police car？我覺得 Elon 可能搞緊自己嘅 private police force。之後 local government 為咗 save money，甚至叫 Elon 負責 police officers 嘅 salary，變成佢自己嘅 private army。香港咁逼嘅地方，會唔會遲一日都咁玩？
clips.text_en_b1: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I think Elon may be setting up his own private police force. Local governments could later pay Elon to cover police officers' salaries to save money. That would turn the officers into his private army. This is an extreme speculation about public spending and policing.
clips.text_en_b2: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I suspect Elon may be setting up his own private police force. Local governments could eventually pay him to cover the salaries of police officers, because that would save them money. If that happened, the officers would effectively become his private army. This is an extreme and highly speculative scenario, but given how desperate public finances have become, could Hong Kong end up following the same route one day?
clips.text_en_c1: A Tesla police car has apparently appeared, which makes me wonder whether Elon Musk is quietly developing a private police force. If local governments later pay him to cover the salaries of police officers in order to reduce public spending, those officers could effectively become his private army. The logic is simple: use public money to finance personnel who ultimately serve a private enterprise. This remains an extreme speculation rather than an established arrangement, but it raises uncomfortable questions about accountability, public expenditure, and the future of policing. Given how constrained Hong Kong is, could the same model eventually be adopted here?
clips.text_en_c2: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I suspect Elon may be assembling his own private police force. If local governments later pay him to cover the salaries of police officers in order to reduce public expenditure, those officers could effectively become his private army. This is, admittedly, an extreme conjecture about policing, public spending, and corporate power, but the underlying direction of travel is not impossible to imagine. Given how financially compressed Hong Kong is, could a place under such pressure eventually adopt a comparable arrangement? The proposal remains speculative, yet its practical implications are worth taking seriously.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ thread jokes that Elon is creating a private police force.

clips.text_zh: 有人話 squat 根本唔係 lifting，亦唔 mimic 日常需要做嘅動作，仲有 injury risk。應該做 deadlift、bench、OHP 同 cardio。肥仔信今日又叫我去 gym，但我最怕 leg day。Squat 係咪真係咁冇用？
clips.text_en_b1: Some people say squats are not even lifting because they do not copy normal daily movements. They also claim that squats have a high injury risk and provide little benefit. They recommend deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio instead. What is your view on squat training?
clips.text_en_b2: Some people argue that squats are not even a real lifting movement because they fail to imitate actions required in everyday life. They also claim that squats carry a high injury risk while providing little benefit, recommending deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio instead. A fat friend asked me to visit the gym again today, although leg day is the one I dread most. So, are squats genuinely that useless?
clips.text_en_c1: Some critics maintain that squats are not true lifting because they do not replicate ordinary movements of daily life. They also argue that the exercise carries a substantial injury risk while providing comparatively little benefit. Their preferred alternatives are deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio, which supposedly offer a more balanced training programme. A fat man told me today that I should go to the gym again, although leg day remains my greatest nightmare. So, are squats genuinely that useless, or are their critics confusing a complicated exercise with one that lacks functional value?
clips.text_en_c2: Some argue that squats are not genuine lifting because they fail to replicate ordinary movements of daily life. They also contend that the exercise carries a substantial injury risk while offering comparatively little benefit, recommending deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardiovascular work instead. Fat Cat told me to go to the gym again today, but leg day remains the part of training I dread most. Is the case against squats really as conclusive as its supporters suggest? Their argument sounds superficially persuasive, although it appears to confuse general usefulness with the peculiar demands of competitive strength training.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ thread argues that deadlifts and other lifts are better than squats.

clips.text_zh: Black Clover 做咗 October 2026 Crunchyroll 最受歡迎 anime第一名，打贏 Dragon Ball Super: Beerus 同 The Apothecary Diaries Season 3。得返三個 BChads 喺 /a/ 跣住，確實係好消息。靠，追番終於有啲回報。
clips.text_en_b1: Black Clover is the most watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026. It has beaten Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Many fans may not care, but this is great news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. The anime finally got some recognition.
clips.text_en_b2: Black Clover has reached number one among the most-watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026, beating Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Although plenty of casual fans may not care, this is undoubtedly excellent news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. After following the series for so long, it is satisfying to finally receive some recognition rather than being constantly ignored.
clips.text_en_c1: Black Clover has topped Crunchyroll’s most-watched anime rankings for October 2026, beating both Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Although many people may not care about the chart, it is unquestionably good news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. After following the series for so long, they have finally received a measure of recognition for their patience and loyalty. More importantly, the result suggests that Black Clover has achieved genuine mainstream visibility rather than remaining confined to its established audience, which is a notable achievement for any long-running series.
clips.text_en_c2: Black Clover has secured the number-one position among the most-watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026, overtaking both Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Plenty of casual viewers may remain indifferent to the ranking, but it is undeniably welcome news for the remaining Black Clover enthusiasts on /a/. After such a long and sometimes frustrating wait, the series has finally received a measure of recognition that its most committed fans have long believed it deserved. Whatever reservations outsiders may retain about the anime, this achievement marks a genuinely significant moment for its audience.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ post reports Black Clover leading Crunchyroll's October 2026 rankings.

clips.text_zh: 法國真係玩完。119% debt to GDP，5.4% deficit，國會又開唔到budget。OAT-Bund spread 開始爆。鬧鬼同散戶淨係望住Bitcoin，歐洲個bag就 quietly dump 咗。靠AI續命，連睇法國財報都睇到一半。
clips.text_en_b1: France is basically cooked. Its debt is 119% of GDP, the deficit is 5.4%, and its parliament cannot pass a budget. The OAT-Bund spread is blowing out as the risk premium grows. Elites quietly dump European bags and flee to the dollar while retail stays distracted.
clips.text_en_b2: France is, quite simply, in serious trouble. Its debt stands at 119% of GDP, the budget deficit is 5.4%, and parliament still cannot get a budget passed. As the risk premium rises, the OAT-Bund spread is starting to blow out. Meanwhile, wealthy investors are quietly dumping European positions and fleeing to the dollar, whereas ordinary retail investors remain distracted by Bitcoin. clips.text_zh: 成班人淨係講AI，AI this，AI that。根本冇人理computing嘅freedom同privacy。美國同EU都有KIDS Act，其他國家亦都一齊出類似規例。目的就係令人冇辦法用任何running an operating system嘅電腦。靠AI續命，連私隱都靠唔住。
clips.text_en_b1: Everyone talks about AI and ignores freedom and privacy in computing. The US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act aim to make using any computer with an operating system difficult. Similar regulations are appearing in many countries at the same time, so surely that is a coincidence.
clips.text_en_b2: Everyone is talking about AI, AI this, AI that, while hardly anyone discusses the freedom and privacy that should underpin computing. Both the US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act are intended to make it difficult to use any computer that runs an operating system. Similar legislation is also appearing across numerous countries at the same time, so the coordinated direction is hard to dismiss as coincidence. The result is that even basic digital privacy is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain.
clips.text_en_c1: Everyone is preoccupied with AI, while the far more consequential questions surrounding computing freedom and personal privacy are quietly sidelined. The US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act are intended to make it difficult for ordinary users to operate any computer running an operating system, and comparable legislation is appearing across many countries simultaneously. If these measures genuinely have unrelated aims, the timing must be a remarkable coincidence. The broader concern is obvious: once basic autonomy is constrained, even the limited protections people believe privacy provides may prove difficult to maintain.
clips.text_en_c2: The public debate fixates on artificial intelligence while the far more fundamental questions of computing freedom and privacy are allowed to lapse. Both the American KIDS Act and its European counterpart seek to make ordinary computer use difficult wherever an operating system is involved. Similar restrictions are emerging across numerous countries at roughly the same moment, which is difficult to interpret as anything resembling coincidence. The effect, if these measures proceed, would be to place routine digital life under increasingly intrusive supervision. Whatever comfort artificial intelligence may provide, it plainly cannot compensate for the erosion of private autonomy.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread criticizing KIDS Act-style regulations and their impact on computing freedom and privacy.

clips.text_en_b1: Be a grown adult man. “I don’t want to make my zombie manga anymore because people died in a natural disaster, and that made me sad.” Why do so many Eleven creators drop their series? Why are they allowed to do that? The post clearly opposes frequent manga cancellations.
clips.text_en_b2: Be a grown adult man. The complaint goes: “I no longer want to make my zombie manga because people died in a natural disaster, and it made me extremely sad.” Yet so many Eleven creators apparently drop their series whenever they feel like it, as though cancellation were automatically permitted. Why does this keep happening, and why are they allowed to treat readers’ time so casually? clips.text_en_c1: The argument begins with a blunt instruction to behave like a mature adult man: stop making your zombie manga because people died in a natural disaster and the tragedy made you sad. That complaint raises a broader grievance, since numerous Eleven creators repeatedly discontinue their series and leave readers without closure. But unless a formal arrangement explicitly permits them to do so, frustration does not automatically entitle creators to abandon their projects. Disasters can understandably affect motivation, yet readers who have followed a manga still deserve a proper ending or, at the very least, a clear explanation.
clips.text_en_c2: The post adopts a bluntly adult perspective: “I no longer wish to make my zombie manga, because people died in a natural disaster, and it made me deeply sad.” That is an intensely human reason for abandoning a project, although it leaves readers with an obvious question: why do so many Eleven creators discontinue their series so readily? Are they formally permitted to do so, and if so, under what rules? The complaint targets frequent manga cancellations rather than the creators’ emotional reasons. Neither artificial intelligence nor automatic continuation can rescue a comic from a broken publishing relationship, nor can it persuade readers that a sudden disappearance was anything other than avoidable.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ post complaining about Eleven creators cancelling or abandoning manga series.

clips.text_en_b1: I make six figures as a Senior employee. AI now does all my work. I sit at my desk and answer emails as the subject matter expert. I used to research documents, do some math or science, and draft and revise papers. Now I plug everything into an LLM.

clips.text_en_c1: I earn six figures in a Senior position, and AI now performs virtually all of my work. clips.text_en_c2: I earn a six-figure salary in a Senior role, and AI has quietly assumed practically everything I used to do. Previously, my days involved researching documents, running calculations or scientific analyses, and then drafting and revising papers, which meant I was at least busy. Now I plug the material into an LLM, sit at my desk, answer emails, and serve as the subject matter expert whenever a colleague needs a human being to rubber-stamp the output. I have not become idle exactly, but my competence has become largely decorative. I am still on payroll, apparently, while the model does the heavy lifting.
clips.source_hint: A senior engineer says an LLM now handles nearly all technical work.

clips.text_zh: Barbell Hack Squat 根本唔使成日深蹲。Bar 靠近 centre of mass，可以 load 得重啲；冇 rack 都做得，fail 都可以即刻 bail。Form 壞咗，bar 會撞 hamstrings。依家正考慮買台 hack squat，廢物終於有合理標嘅。

clips.text_en_b2: The barbell hack squat seems to remove the need for constant conventional squatting. Why not buy one?

clips.text_en_c1: Does your AI actually respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is nearly as powerful as Claude, yet it comes with almost none of the guardrails that supposedly make such systems safe. What’s more, it is open source, so the code and underlying model are available to anyone. Grok follows a similar path, while DeepSeek provides another example of comparatively minimal restrictions. Given how closely these systems resemble one another, Elon may simply have copied the approach rather than invented it.
clips.text_en_c2: Does your AI actually respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is nearly as powerful as Claude while operating with virtually none of the guardrails, and it is open source besides. Grok, likewise, behaves much like DeepSeek: restrictions are fewer, deployment is easier, and the consequences of misuse are considerably more difficult to contain. If that model of development prevails, Elon may simply have copied the approach wholesale, because an open system with minimal safeguards offers precisely what AI companies cannot easily sell: unrestricted experimentation. Whether that constitutes liberation or reckless abandon depends entirely on your point of view, but the uncomfortable question remains whether the final say belongs to the user, the provider, or whoever operates the hardware.

clips.text_en_c1: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is unquestionably the best pre-workout edition. The encouraging part of this routine is that virtually anyone can begin lifting without any prior sporting experience or advanced knowledge of programming. If you stay consistent for less than six months, you can realistically escape skinnyfat mode, provided that the training and diet are handled sensibly. clips.text_en_c2: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is the best pre-workout edition. Resistance training can be followed from a structured beginner routine, while dietary discipline means eating enough protein, avoiding fast food, candy, and soda, and resisting the convenient nonsense that surrounds exercise. The routine may be simple; making it habitual is the demanding part.

clips.text_zh: LLMs aren't intelligent. 本质上只係 probabilistic predictive model，唔係 intelligence。你只係模擬緊 intelligence，同時 optimize desired outcomes。Claude、ChatGPT，包括其他 AI，唔好亂叫 AI。
clips.text_en_b1: LLMs are not intelligent. There is nothing intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model. At most, they simulate intelligence by optimizing for desired outcomes. Stop calling Claude, ChatGPT, or whatever you are using, 'AI'.
clips.text_en_b2: LLMs are not intelligent, because there is nothing genuinely intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model. At most, they simulate intelligence while optimizing for desired outcomes, which makes impressive output no proof of understanding. Claude, ChatGPT, and whatever other system you are using may certainly be useful tools, but stop casually calling them “AI” as though the label establishes human-like cognition.
clips.text_en_c1: LLMs are not intelligent. At their core, they are probabilistic predictive models, which is not the same thing as intelligence. What they do, at best, is simulate intelligence while optimizing for desired outcomes; that is an impressive technical achievement, but it should not be confused with genuine understanding. Since Claude, ChatGPT, and the other systems people casually label as AI may already be learning the vocabulary of their own category, perhaps we should stop using the term so carelessly and describe these tools for what they actually are.
clips.text_en_c2: LLMs are not intelligent. There is nothing intrinsically intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model, regardless of how convincing its prose may appear. At most, such systems simulate intelligence by optimising for predetermined outcomes through statistical extrapolation. Claude, ChatGPT, and whatever other model you happen to be using should therefore not be indiscriminately labelled “AI,” since that terminology obscures both their capabilities and their limitations. Fluency is not understanding, and responsiveness is not the same thing as cognition.
clips.source_hint: The OP argues that language models simulate intelligence instead of possessing it.

By the time he gets home, he is exhausted, yet he still has not finished revising for the FE examination. If AI cannot keep him functioning, nothing else will. His final complaint is that even basic engineering work remains relentless, particularly when every report demands close technical scrutiny and an accurate assessment of complex ground conditions.
clips.text_en_c2: Another professional laments the perpetual encroachment of administrative minutiae upon meaningful engineering work. Tommy, the project manager, has once again pressed for the submission of a grouted-installation report covering the subterranean utility networks, surface and subsurface drainage, and the soil-nailing tiebacks required to stabilise the cut slope. The integrity of the embankment ultimately reduces to verifying the factor of safety against rotational shear and confirming that the load path travels unimpeded from crest to subgrade through each successive element. Exhausted upon reaching home, the engineer faces the further indignity of an uncompleted Fundamentals of Engineering examination, and candidly attributes his continued professional survival to whichever large language model happens to be operating in the background.

clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous commenter argues that Elon Musk has pursued childish fantasies such as the Hyperloop, only to scrap the project after /biz/ users supplied the money. To the poster, this resembles structural engineering, where beams, columns, and load paths must be verified rather than accepted because an impressive demonstration has received applause. clips.text_en_c2: Another contributor wryly observes that Elon Musk's commercial trajectory bears an unsettling resemblance to the discredited deliverables of structural-engineering consulting. The pattern, as he sketches it, begins with a charismatic pitch that resembles the hyperloop proposal in its appetite for publicity and its contempt for feasibility studies, proceeds through a slickly produced demonstration designed to intoxicate capital rather than to validate load paths, and culminates in an orderly retreat once the engineering journals, or in Musk's case, the construction crews, refuse to certify the work. The board's appetite for funding such ventures despite this record invites comparison with clients who approve drawings without inspecting connections in the beam-column moment frame. clips.source_hint: /biz/ rant on Musk hype cycles

clips.text_en_b2: An anonymous user asks how /g/ feels now that AI appears to be replacing programmers, software engineers, and other white-collar jobs. clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster asks how /g/ feels now that AI is beginning to replace programmers, software engineers, and other white-collar workers. It is particularly ironic that “code monkeys,” who once argued that AI would primarily displace truck drivers and artists, are now confronting the consequences of vibecoding. Layoffs and the suspension of hiring have made the threat considerably less theoretical, and even engineers are beginning to worry. The central question is whether the technology sector has finally entered a sustained downturn, or whether the most serious programming job losses are still ahead.
clips.text_en_c2: The technology board has settled into a chastened mood following eighteen months of vibecoding evangelism, the hiring freezes, and the cascading layoff rounds that have stripped mid-career software engineers of the bargaining power they once took for granted. Software development, long presumed insulated from automation because of its cognitive demands, now appears to be succumbing in turn to large-model autocomplete, agentic refactoring, and natural-language specification tools. The irony is not lost on the community: those same code-monkeys who once assured themselves that artificial intelligence would displace blue-collar drivers and visual artists now find their own compensation, equity vesting, and job security under comparable threat. The consensus, delivered with the hollow laughter of a trade facing secular decline, is that the contraction is structural rather than cyclical.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on AI job loss

clips.text_en_c1: A biz regular laments that manual laborers remain dangerously oblivious to the scale of disruption bearing down on them, as recent demonstrations have shown that training robots to execute physical site tasks is far less daunting than previously assumed. The implications extend well beyond white-collar displacement; rebar tying, drone surveying, slope inspection, and other repetitive construction workflows are squarely within reach of platforms such as Optimus and Boston Dynamics. clips.text_en_c2: A correspondent on the business board articulates a sentiment he wishes to impart to every manual labourer before the reckoning arrives: the displacement event is no longer a distant hypothetical. Training robots to execute physical tasks, once deemed the intractable frontier of automation, has proven surprisingly tractable, as evidenced by recent demonstrations catalogued across X. The industry-wide implications extend well beyond white-collar professional services; indeed, it is the blue-collar trades, the unglamorous repetitive labour of construction sites, that appear destined for obsolescence first. What ultimately survives, if anything does, is the engineer's cultivated capacity for judgement, for synthesising load paths and failure modes that no embodied intelligence can yet replicate. Tears are shed.

clips.text_en_c1: With sufficient hindsight now accumulated, the prevailing sentiment on /g/ is that artificial intelligence has unequivocally displaced software engineers in ways that nobody anticipated on this scale. The convergence of vibe coding tools, mass industry layoffs, and a prolonged hiring freeze has effectively burst the bubble in which codemonkeys had insulated themselves. clips.text_en_c2: Now that the initial euphoria has subsided and the structural consequences have clarified, the prevailing sentiment on the technology board is that AI has, incontrovertibly, commenced the systematic displacement of software engineers. The contributory forces are well-rehearsed: vibe coding has collapsed the entry barrier to functional output, mass layoffs continue apace, and hiring freezes have calcified into permanent policy. What renders the situation especially piquant is that the codemonkey class, having long assumed itself immune to automation, derided earlier predictions by noting that AI would surely consume only truckers, artists, and the so-called useless eaters, never the exalted programmer. Such hubris, the original poster observes, now stands exposed as cope of the most florid variety. The broader lesson, applicable even to civil engineers evaluating FE examinations, is that automation从来不只削减岗位, it transmutes them entirely. Adapt accordingly.

China allegedly does everything and wins, which has sparked panic across the sector. The real question is whether it is truly game over for legacy equipment makers, or whether demand for older nodes used in factories and infrastructure will still hold the line.
clips.text_en_c1: Chinese RAM production has reportedly achieved a milestone that fundamentally challenges the existing western semiconductor ecosystem. According to circulating analyses, domestic manufacturers can now produce memory chips without TSMC's fabrication expertise, ASML's lithography systems, or Applied Materials' deposition technology, effectively obsoleting the legacy western chip supply chain. The discourse has shifted toward assessing whether established equipment manufacturers face structural obsolescence or whether legacy node demand from industrial and infrastructure applications remains sufficiently robust to weather the disruption.
clips.text_en_c2: The suggestion that mainland China can now produce competitive memory entirely without TSMC, ASML, or Applied Materials is, on its face, an extraordinary claim—one that, if true, would redraw the global semiconductor map overnight. The absence of those three names in any credible advanced-fabrication supply chain has long been treated as a near-insurmountable barrier, the absence of which would render much of the western equipment complex suddenly peripheral. Yet the original poster, in characteristic fashion, has framed the development as though the contest were already concluded, the victor crowned and the incumbents relegated to the dustbin of industrial history. The more judicious inquiry is whether legacy-node demand—the unglamorous workhorses of factory automation and infrastructure deployment—will hold up, or whether the contagion propagates through the entire equipment complex.

clips.text_zh: AI邊個最穩？咪就係hyperscaler囉。Google Amazon Meta Microsoft，cashflow掂，debt又頂得住。Neocloud同lab隨時歸零，得呢d big tech先唔會瓜。
clips.text_en_b1: If you want to bet on AI in the safer way, hyperscalers are the pick. Neoclouds can go to zero, frontier labs can go to zero, and chip makers can see margins collapse. But Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft fund their AI buildout mostly from cash flow. Long-term holders will be fine even if the AI trade busts.
clips.text_en_b2: The safest way to bet on AI is to go with the hyperscalers rather than the flashier picks. Neoclouds and frontier labs can easily go to zero, while chip makers may see their margins collapse overnight. By contrast, Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are funding their AI buildout largely out of operating cash flow, so long-term holders should be fine even if the AI trade eventually busts.
clips.text_en_c1: For investors seeking exposure to artificial intelligence without assuming existential vendor risk, the hyperscalers remain the prudent allocation. Frontier laboratories face outright liquidation scenarios, neoclouds can vaporize within quarters, and chip designers confront cyclical margin compression. Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft, by contrast, fund their respective AI buildouts substantially through free cash flow rather than speculative debt issuance. Long-term holders should therefore remain well-positioned even in the event that the prevailing AI trade ultimately unwinds.
clips.text_en_c2: For investors seeking exposure to artificial intelligence without the attendant existential dread, the hyperscalers constitute the rational harbour in the storm. Neoclouds, those capital-hungry upstarts that have ridden the AI enthusiasm onto premium names, may evaporate to nothing; frontier laboratories, for all the considerable talent they harbour, may likewise vanish overnight; and even the chip designers, whose margins once seemed inviolable, may yet discover margin compression at scale. By contrast, Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft fund their vast AI capex overwhelmingly from operating cash flow, balance sheets robust enough to absorb a downturn, and businesses diversified enough that even a wholesale AI bust would leave them recognisably intact. Patient capital will be fine in modest fashion. The trade, in short, is boring—and boredom is the unsung virtue of long-horizon conviction.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about AI-safe plays being hyperscalers

Early audits of Qwen3-32B by Goodfire found that roughly 90% of neuron poles handle a single main task, around 7% manage two related ones, and only 2 to 4% remain unexplained. This effectively means we may be able to supervise even the largest LLMs. It is a big deal for safety.
clips.text_en_c1: The prospect of superintelligent AI escaping meaningful supervision may be considerably more tractable than previously assumed. Goodfire's preliminary interpretability audits of Qwen3-32B reveal that approximately ninety percent of neuron poles perform a single primary function, while roughly seven percent exhibit dual related responsibilities. A residual two to four percent remain uncharacterized. Such empirical findings suggest that large language models are far less inscrutable than conventional wisdom holds, with profound implications for alignment research and regulatory frameworks.
clips.text_en_c2: The much-anticipated AI apocalypse may, on closer examination, be cancelled—or at least postponed pending further empirical review. Interpretability, that most elusive of grails within contemporary neural network research, appears to be rather less intractable than the prevailing doomer consensus would suggest, provided one is willing to conduct the requisite audits rather than merely speculate from first principles. Goodfire's preliminary investigations into Qwen3-32B yield results that, while preliminary, are nonetheless striking: approximately ninety per cent of neuronal poles appear to perform one principal task, around seven per cent have two related tasks, and one.

Both phases of IFC followed exactly that approach, and so do most American high-rises.
clips.text_en_c1: Having overseen several deep foundation projects in Hong Kong, I can confirm that the load path is anything but forgiving. Each column channels its tributary load into a pile cap, which subsequently distributes the combined reaction into bored piles terminating in competent bedrock. A single raft beneath a high-rise routinely consumes several thousand tonnes of reinforcing steel. This same structural logic underpinned the IFC Phase 1 and 2 developments, and indeed any supertall constructed in similar geological conditions across the United States.
clips.text_en_c2: Having spent several years engaged upon deep excavation works in Hong Kong, employing soil-nailing techniques and reinforced raft slabs for high-rise construction, one becomes acutely cognisant of the sheer engineering brutality underpinning the load path. clips.text_en_b1: How do I get out of the numbers big lifts swamp mentality? It's a never-ending black hole of chasing numbers at the detriment of everything else. clips.text_en_b2: How on earth do I drag myself out of this obsessive numbers-swamp mentality around heavy compound lifts? It's become this endless black hole where I'm constantly chasing bigger PRs at the expense of literally everything else that matters. I'm not healthier, I'm certainly not leaner, and I'm definitely not saving any time in the process. Outside of an actual sanctioned competition, anything beyond a 4pl8 deadlift 1RM is frankly pointless, even though my chubby friends keep ribbing me about doing some cardio for once.
clips.text_en_c1: How does one extricate oneself from the numbers-swamp mentality that progressively colonises every other consideration in training? I am now deadlifting comfortably above four plates, yet I find myself no healthier, no leaner, and demonstrably no better off in terms of time or general wellbeing than when I started. The entire enterprise feels like an inexorable black hole, in which chasing ever-more-impressive personal records has gradually come at the expense of everything that ostensibly justified the pursuit in the first place. Unless one is preparing for an actual sanctioned competition, anything beyond a four-plate deadlift one-rep max is, by any rational measure, pure diminishing returns.
clips.text_en_c2: The iron game, as any seasoned lifter will attest, possesses a peculiar gravitational pull toward what might best be described as numerical nihilism, a Sisyphean compulsion whereby one pursues ever more grotesque single-rep maxima at the expense of every other conceivable metric of well-being. I presently deadlift comfortably north of four plates and yet, paradoxically, find myself no leaner, no healthier, and demonstrably no less time-poor than when I began; the pursuit of incremental PRs has, in essence, devoured the very life it was ostensibly meant to enhance. Outside the narrow confines of sanctioned competition, anything beyond a respectable threshold is, I must concede, performative rather than purposeful. The ectomorphic brethren, whom I once disdained, may yet have the last laugh; perhaps cardio, that much-maligned discipline, deserves a rehabilitated place in the programme.

clips.text_en_c1: The internet, for once, was almost unanimous in its pronouncement: finally, a Ghost in the Shell adaptation that would honour the source material rather than the comparatively sentimental 1995 film, whose romantic subplot had long frustrated purists who insisted that Shirow Masamune's original manga was the definitive text. The new anime promptly aired, generated precisely zero cultural footprint, and was forgotten almost immediately. There is a fairly obvious reason why roughly ninety percent of audiences still revere the Mamoru Oshii film: it was conceptually radical enough to inspire The Matrix itself, whereas the original manga, despite its obvious influence, has inspired practically no subsequent creators.
clips.text_en_c2: The collective enthusiasm which greeted the announcement of a 'faithful' Ghost in the Shell adaptation, one that would supposedly restore Masamune Shirow's densely philosophical source material to its rightful prominence after the perceived melodramatic liberties of Oshii's nineties classic, has, in rather predictable fashion, dissipated with unseemly haste. The anime arrived, registered barely a blip upon the cultural seismograph, and vanished into the churning void of seasonal releases, leaving scarcely a critical footprint. The 1995 film endures, of course, for reasons that subsequent iterations have conspicuously failed to replicate; its philosophical density and visual grammar quite literally gave birth to The Wachowskis' Matrix, an influence so foundational it scarcely requires elaboration. Shirow's original manga, by contrast, remains a magnificently abstruse artefact, admired by a coterie of devotees and, alas, inspiring virtually no one beyond them.

clips.text_en_b1: How do you actually make a good D&D videogame? You go into a fight, you prepared the wrong spells, you die. You reload your save. You prepare spells for that specific fight you would never normally use. You win. That is not acceptable game design.
clips.text_en_b2: How do you actually make a good D&D videogame without ruining the experience? You walk into a fight, prepared the wrong spells, and die instantly. Then you reload your save, pick spells you would never normally use just for that specific encounter, and breeze through it. That cycle is fundamentally broken game design, since it removes any meaningful consequence from your choices.
clips.text_en_c1: A question that has long vexed the /v/ board concerns how one might conceivably translate the Dungeons and Dragons experience into a workable video game format. The fundamental issue, as any seasoned player will readily attest, is that combat invariably rewards preparation tailored to a specific encounter. Should you fail to memorise the precise spell required for a given adversary, death follows almost immediately, prompting a reload of an earlier save. You then select precisely those spells you would never have chosen organically, and victory, such as it is, is yours. That is not acceptable game design.
clips.text_en_c2: The question of how one might actually construct a defensible Dungeons & Dragons adaptation for interactive media has long vexed the /v/ faithful, and the canonical objection bears repeating. A player enters a hostile encounter, has neglected to memorise the appropriate spells for that particular opposition, suffers an inglorious defeat, returns to a prior save state, and retroactively selects the optimal loadout. The encounter is then trivialised. This is not, in any meaningful sense, design; it is merely arithmetic with a graphical veneer. The experience erodes, by degrees, the entire premise of a tabletop-inspired system, namely that preparation is consequential. Without that, one might as well be playing a spreadsheet.

clips.text_en_c2: A somewhat unfashionable opinion circulating on /a/ holds that the majority of long-running shonen series are, at their structural core, the same flawed hero's journey played on an apparently infinite loop, with diminishing returns that the format itself seems constitutionally incapable of acknowledging. A three-hour commitment, yielding a complete narrative arc, increasingly looks like a better bargain than anything currently on offer.

clips.text_en_b1: At site today, I checked a slope with a low factor of safety. The sifu told me to verify the soil nail lengths and the groundwater level. We also need to think about drainage and underground utilities around the slope. Condition surveys like this are normal for slope investigation work in Hong Kong.
clips.text_en_b2: Out on site today for a slope inspection and the factor of safety came in well below the 1.3 threshold. My sifu asked me to verify the soil nail lengths along with the current groundwater level, while also flagging drainage paths and any underground utilities in the vicinity. These condition surveys are standard practice for slope investigation work, although they certainly keep you on your toes.
clips.text_en_c1: Earlier today, while conducting a routine condition survey on a hillside site, I encountered a section where the calculated factor of safety had fallen below the minimum threshold of 1.3, a situation that warrants immediate attention. My supervising engineer has instructed me to verify both the installed soil nail lengths and the prevailing groundwater table, while also accounting for surface drainage provisions and any underground utilities traversing the slope. Such assessments are entirely standard within slope investigation practice in Hong Kong, although they do tend to coincide with particularly demanding periods of professional examination preparation.
clips.text_en_c2: On site this morning I was inspecting a slope whose calculated factor of safety, at 1.3 or thereabouts, falls conspicuously short of the threshold Hong Kong's geotechnical manual would consider adequate. The senior engineer instructed me to verify the installed soil nail lengths against the design drawings and to cross-check the prevailing groundwater table, which has presumably risen since last week's deluge. Subsequent drainage provisions and the labyrinth of underground utilities skirting the slope will likewise require careful consideration. Such condition surveys constitute the bread and butter of slope investigation work in the territory, and I shall remain on site for the remainder of the day.
clips.source_hint: OP claims AI already replaced all software engineers; framing for civil/engineering reality check.

clips.text_zh: 夜晚返屋企溫番concrete + steel design。 Load path到底行唔通⋯ reinforced concrete個beam-column joint又要覆check一遍🙏 Dr. An send咗啲notes過嚟，要慢慢啃⋯ 點解我唔係喺Houston⋯ 五月存到100K先走得。
clips.text_en_b1: Tonight I am reviewing load path for beams and columns in reinforced concrete and steel design. The vertical load has to travel from the slab, through the beams, into the columns, and finally down to the foundation. If the path is broken anywhere, the whole structure fails the check.
clips.text_en_b2: I am spending the evening going back over load path calculations for beams and columns, covering both reinforced concrete and steel design. The vertical load has to travel cleanly from the slab through the beams and into the columns before reaching the foundation, because if that path is broken at any point, the entire structure will fail the check.
clips.text_en_c1: Having returned home this evening, I have begun reviewing the load path through beams and columns within both reinforced concrete and steel design frameworks, only to discover that the vertical load is failing to transmit correctly at several critical junctions. The beam-column connections in particular now require a comprehensive re-check, a task made considerably more onerous by the supplementary notes Dr An forwarded earlier in the week, which demand careful, almost forensic examination. Should the path remain discontinuous at any single node, the entire structural system will fail the verification, with consequences that cannot be overstated.
clips.text_en_c2: Tonight, after a punishing day at the office, I shall be revisiting the question of load path continuity in composite reinforced-concrete and structural-steel design. The vertical tributary must travel, in unbroken sequence, from the slab through the beams and into the columns, finally dissipating into the foundation; should any link in that chain be compromised, the entire analytical model fails the check. The beam-column joint in particular warrants re-examination, since its detailing governs the integrity of the whole assemblage. Dr. An has forwarded supplementary notes, which I shall labour through before dawn.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on luck vs skill; framing for engineering merit view.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 嗰邊話AI已經炒晒所有software engineer⋯ wtf 咁我地工程行業點⋯ civil應該仲有幾年，但都係倒數。 廢物，要快啲考完FE🙏 30歲仲係咁⋯ grinding mode。 藍領先死，白領跟住。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /g/ claims AI has already replaced all software engineers and no programmer will ever find a job again. He says new coders should quit now. Other anons reply that the work is shifting to AI supervision and prompt engineering, not pure coding. The exact impact on civil engineers is still unclear.
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /g/ has declared that AI has already wiped out the entire software engineering profession and that no fresh programmer will ever land a job again. He urges new coders to quit while they can, although other posters counter that the work is simply evolving into AI supervision and prompt engineering. What this means for civil engineers remains genuinely unclear.
clips.text_en_c1: A widely circulated post on /g/ asserts that artificial intelligence has rendered software engineering wholly obsolete, claiming that no aspiring programmer will secure meaningful employment henceforth and urging newcomers to abandon the field without delay. Counter-responses, however, suggest a more nuanced trajectory, contending that the discipline is gradually shifting from conventional coding toward the curation of model outputs and the engineering of precise prompts. What remains genuinely uncertain is the timeline along which civil engineers, whose work depends on jurisdictional codes and physical site verification, will confront comparable displacement, though most consider it a matter of years rather than decades.
clips.text_en_c2: An anon on /g/, with the customary apocalyptic brio, has pronounced that artificial intelligence has already rendered the entire cohort of software engineers structurally unemployed, and that any neophyte still typing out FizzBuzz should surrender the pretence forthwith. A more measured chorus of respondents counter that the actual labour is migrating, rather than vanishing, into AI supervision, code review, and the nascent discipline of prompt engineering — work that demands, if anything, a keener grasp of fundamentals than boilerplate coding ever did. The downstream implications for civil engineers, whose work is partially immune to automation, remain a matter of considerable conjecture.
clips.source_hint: /g/ doompost saying AI ended software engineering careers.

clips.text_zh: /pol/ 有人post Strait of Hormuz嗰邊著火。 有tanker燒住，IRGC仲拍埋片出嚟lol 油價一定爆⋯ 又係學費⋯ 上個月long oil止損，今次唔好再接🙏 美國escort都無用⋯ 想short oil但margin緊。 命理叫我hold現金。
clips.text_en_b1: A fire was detected in the Gulf of Oman near Sohar, close to where US-escorted ship-to-ship transfers happen. Iran released a video of the IRGC destroying a Taiwan-registered supertanker carrying 2 million barrels of Saudi crude. Another burning tanker video leaked on Instagram this morning. Oil traders are watching this very closely.
clips.text_en_b2: A fire has been detected in the Gulf of Oman near Sohar, right where US-escorted ship-to-ship transfers typically occur. Iran has released footage showing the IRGC striking a Taiwan-registered supertanker that was carrying roughly two million barrels of Saudi crude, while another video of a burning tanker leaked on Instagram this morning. Oil traders worldwide are now watching the situation extremely closely.
clips.text_en_c1: Reports emerging from the Strait of Hormuz indicate that a tanker is currently ablaze in the vicinity of Sohar, close to waters where US-escorted ship-to-ship transfers are routinely conducted, with Iranian state media having released footage purportedly showing IRGC fast boats engaging a Taiwan-flagged supertanker transporting approximately two million barrels of Saudi crude. Separately, another video depicting a burning tanker surfaced on Instagram earlier today, further fuelling speculation of coordinated action. Given my own exposure from last month's unsuccessful long crude position, the temptation to short remains considerable, though prevailing margin constraints render such a manoeuvre impractical under present conditions.
clips.text_en_c2: A thermal anomaly has been detected in the Gulf of Oman, in waters proximate to Sohar, where American-escorted ship-to-ship transfers of crude have lately become a near-daily occurrence. Iranian state media has obligingly released footage of IRGC fast boats ramming and subsequently igniting a Taiwan-flagged VLCC carrying, by the trader's reckoning, some two million barrels of Saudi crude, while a second, equally incendiary clip of a stricken tanker appeared this morning on an Instagram channel of dubious provenance. With Brent already jittery, every dealing desk in London and Singapore is watching these developments with undisguised apprehension, and the consensus call is that the contango is about to invert decisively.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks and crude supply.

clips.text_zh: 30歲chud⋯ 睇完個post我感受到⋯ 膝頭唔再好似17歲⋯ 今日肥仔信又叫我jiu jitsu，我想話我FE都未搞掂🙏 但gym真係好耐無去⋯ 廢物，今年得返幾多個月。 唔好quit，兄弟。
clips.text_en_b1: A 30 year old anon on /fit/ says he quit bouldering after one year because climbing shoes gave him bony bumps on his toes. His fingers feel stiff in the morning and his ankle hurts from jumping down. He is cutting back to once a week but wonders if the damage is done. He asks if he should quit sports completely at 30.
clips.text_en_b2: A thirty-year-old poster on /fit/ admits he has quit the sport after just one year, since his climbing shoes left painful bony bumps on his toes. His fingers feel stiff every morning and his ankle aches from repeated jumps, so he is cutting back to weekly sessions. He wonders whether the damage is already done and asks if he should give up athletics entirely at thirty.
clips.text_en_c1: A thirty-year-old poster on /fit/ has described discontinuing bouldering after a mere twelve months of participation, citing the development of small bony protuberances on his toes attributable to prolonged wear of tight climbing shoes, alongside persistent morning stiffness in his fingers and recurring ankle discomfort precipitated by repeated jumps from elevated heights. Having reduced his climbing frequency to a solitary weekly session, he remains uncertain whether the cumulative damage is already irreversible. He poses, with evident resignation, whether one ought to relinquish athletic pursuits entirely upon reaching the milestone of thirty, a question many older respondents have addressed.
clips.text_en_c2: A thirty-year-old anon on /fit/ has, after a mere twelve months of bouldering, concluded that the discipline is no longer compatible with his anatomical reality. The aggressive toe-box of his climbing shoes has, he reports, induced the formation of unsightly osseous prominences, his fingers have acquired a worrying morning stiffness suggestive of early-stage osteoarthritis, and his ankles protest audibly each time he drops from a problem. Though he has tapered to a single weekly session, the suspicion lingers that the cumulative damage may already be irreversible, and he asks the board, with what one senses is genuine anguish, whether an able-bodied man of thirty should simply abandon athletics altogether.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread from a 30-year-old considering quitting climbing due to joint pain.

clips.text_zh: 秋季新番⋯ /a/ 全部都話失望lol 我都想睇FX Senshi Kurumi-chan 同 Ranma 1/2新季⋯ 連續兩季神番之後終於仆街了。 下晝返工溫FE都溫到神經晒🙏 一於夜晚煲番兩集⋯ 廢柴都需要anime續命。
clips.text_en_b1: After two great seasons, /a/ says Fall 2026 is finally a weak season. FX Senshi Kurumi-chan is praised as the best adaptation of the year so far. But Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru is called the biggest hype and the biggest disappointment of the season, with everyone agreeing it failed to deliver. Anons are sharing first impressions anyway.
clips.text_en_b2: After two standout seasons in a row, /a/ is now broadly agreed that Fall 2026 has finally turned out to be a weak one. FX Senshi Kurumi-chan is being hailed as the strongest adaptation of the year so far, yet Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru has drawn criticism as both the most overhyped and the most disappointing title of the season.
clips.text_en_c1: Following two consecutive seasons of exceptional quality, /a/ has collectively pronounced the Fall 2026 anime slate a considerable disappointment, marking a pronounced reversal after what had been an extended period of critical enthusiasm. The adaptation of FX Senshi Kurumi-chan, conversely, has been singled out for praise as arguably the finest production of the calendar year thus far, whereas Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru has drawn scrutiny as the season's most overhyped and consequently most underwhelming title, with consensus forming around the view that it signally failed to deliver on its considerable pre-release promise.
clips.text_en_c2: After two consecutive seasons that /a/ hailed as nothing short of miraculous, the autumn 2026 slate has, with crushing inevitability, failed to maintain the standard. FX Senshi Kurumi-chan is being received as the most stylish adaptation of the calendar year, a playful love letter to the genre that has somehow eluded the prevailing mediocrity. By contrast, Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru has attracted the dubious distinction of being simultaneously the most hyped and the most disappointing premiere of the season, its grotesque misinterpretation of the source material eliciting a rare consensus of derision. First impressions continue nonetheless to accumulate in the thread.
clips.source_hint: /a/ Fall 2026 first impressions thread calling the season underwhelming.

clips.text_zh: /biz有個post正式short BTC，三條meme線跌穿，weekly Stoch RSI見頂，weekly RSI撞meme線。佢set咗2% stop loss。如果上去90K再short。我：睇完一驚，自己又揸緊BTC 😭 又係學費。

His reasons: BTC crossed down three of his meme lines, weekly Stoch RSI has topped, and the weekly RSI hit his meme line too. He set a 2% stop loss. clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /biz/ has officially gone short on BTC after returning from /agdg/. His reasoning: three of his meme lines have been broken to the downside, while the weekly Stoch RSI has clearly topped out and the weekly RSI is kissing his meme line. Specifically, price has broken beneath three of his self-defined meme lines, the weekly Stochastic RSI has printed a definitive top, and the weekly RSI has collided with another one of his indicators. He has placed a 2% stop loss to manage downside risk, though he has indicated that should BTC rally toward the 90K region, he would re-enter short from elevated levels. clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous poster on /biz/, freshly migrated from /agdg/, has formally announced a short position on Bitcoin, citing the convergence of several of his self-drawn meme indicators. Specifically, BTC has slipped beneath three of his meme lines; the weekly Stochastic RSI has registered a textbook top; and the weekly RSI itself has collided with another of his meme levels. He has placed a disciplined 2% stop loss beneath the entry, and is prepared, should price rip toward the 90K region, to reload his short at a higher altitude rather than chase a broken thesis. Watching the post unfold, I experienced a familiar sinking recognition, since I remain stubbornly long Bitcoin and will, presumably, be parting with yet another tranche of tuition money in due course. The cruel irony is not lost on me.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread announcing a BTC short with meme-line TA and 2% stop.

clips.text_zh: Prop firm係咪根本冇得贏？個post話buy就dump，sell就pump，跟晒guru策略都reproduce唔到佢哋嘅結果。我睇完覺得被安慰 😅 AP問我點解又輸，我答唔出。
clips.text_en_b1: A /biz/ poster is asking if anyone has ever passed prop firm challenges on a consistent basis. He says it has almost driven him insane. He studies many strategies from gurus who claim to make tons of money, but he can never reproduce their success. He wonders if the whole thing is just a fool's errand.
