clips.text_en_b2: A /biz/ poster is questioning whether prop firm challenges can actually be passed on a consistent basis. He admits the grind has nearly driven him insane, since he has studied countless guru strategies claiming massive returns yet fails to reproduce any of their results. He wonders if the whole pursuit is essentially a fool's errand. Reading this was oddly comforting, because my own P&L this month tells exactly the same story. Could not even answer when AP asked why I lost again.
clips.text_en_c1: A frustrated /biz/ contributor has posed the question of whether anyone has ever consistently passed proprietary trading firm challenges, suggesting that the endeavour has pushed him to the brink of sanity. He elaborates that, despite meticulously studying numerous strategies disseminated by self-proclaimed gurus who flaunt extraordinary returns, he cannot replicate their claimed performance. The implication is that the entire enterprise may amount to nothing more than a fool's errand, a Sisyphean pursuit designed to separate aspirants from their capital. Resonating uncomfortably with my own P&L statements this month, I find myself unable to offer a satisfactory answer when acquaintances inquire why I have haemorrhaged money yet again.
clips.text_en_c2: A /biz/ contributor has posed what may be the thread's most uncomfortable question: has anyone, anywhere, ever cleared a prop firm evaluation on a genuinely consistent basis? He confesses the pursuit has brought him to the brink of sanity, poring over the proprietary strategies of self-styled gurus who flaunt screenshots of obscene returns, only to find that none of their methods can be faithfully reproduced in live markets. He is beginning to suspect the entire enterprise is an elaborate fool's errand, a confidence game dressed in risk management. The sentiment lands with surgical precision upon my own recent ledger; if asked by my account partner why the month ended in red, I would struggle to formulate a coherent defence. Read the post; weep quietly.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about the impossibility of passing prop firm challenges.

clips.text_zh: 有/biz仔自稱係最大bull，話依家係black swan event，最差嘅bond bear market in history。對我嚟講同slope一樣，factor of safety跌晒，要revisit成個load path。
clips.text_en_b1: A self-described biggest bull on /biz/ is calling the current move a black swan event. He says the bond bear market is becoming the worst in history. He admits it sounds bearish to most people, but he frames it as bullish overall. For me this feels like a slope with the factor of safety gone, every load path needs to be rechecked.
clips.text_en_b2: A self-proclaimed biggest bull on /biz/ is framing the current move as a black swan event, claiming the bond bear market is shaping up to be the worst in history. Although this sounds bearish on the surface, he insists the broader picture remains bullish. For me the situation feels like a slope whose factor of safety has completely vanished. Every load path now needs revisiting, and honestly I am not sure any of it holds together anymore.
clips.text_en_c1: A self-styled contrarian on /biz/, who routinely identifies as the foremost bull, has characterised the prevailing market dislocation as a bona fide black swan event. He contends that the ongoing bond bear market is on course to become the most severe in recorded financial history, an assertion which, paradoxically, he interprets as bullish rather than bearish, provided one possesses the appropriate macro framework. For my part, the current environment evokes the unsettling sensation of standing on a slope whose factor of safety has evaporated entirely, demanding that every conceivable load path be painstakingly revisited before any further commitment of capital.
clips.text_en_c2: A self-proclaimed arch-bull on /biz/ has grudgingly conceded that the prevailing bond rout constitutes, in his estimation, a genuine black swan event and is rapidly asserting itself as the most punishing bond bear market in recorded financial history. Although the framing sounds emphatically bearish to any casual observer, he insists the dislocation must ultimately be interpreted as constructively bullish for risk assets further out the timeline. The structural analogy is rather apt: one is essentially watching a slope whose factor of safety has been quietly eroded, where every conventional load path now demands a thorough re-examination and the margin against catastrophic failure has thinned beyond what any prudent engineer would accept. The terrain, in other words, warrants considerable circumspection.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread warning that the bond bear market is the worst in history.

clips.text_zh: /biz有post話wood比gold更稀有，外星人嚟地球都係偷wood唔係偷gold。同reinforced concrete一樣，concrete supply穩陣過steel先係common sense lol。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon claims wood is the rarest material in the universe, rarer than gold or diamonds. He says if aliens invade Earth they will steal wood, not gold or silver. He argues gold is abundant inside the earth and worthless. A structural take: like reinforced concrete, supply matters more than hype.
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /biz/ insists wood is rarer than gold or diamonds, joking that any aliens invading Earth would come for timber rather than bullion, since gold sits abundantly inside the planet and is essentially worthless. While the take is deliberately absurd, the underlying logic resonates. Reinforced concrete teaches the same lesson: stable supply chains beat hype every single time. Common sense, apparently, is not so common.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /biz/ has advanced the provocative thesis that wood constitutes the rarest material in the known universe, surpassing even gold or diamonds in scarcity. Extending the argument into the realm of speculative cosmology, he posits that any extraterrestrial civilisation intent on plundering Earth would logically target timber rather than precious metals, dismissing gold as volumetrically abundant within the planet's crust and therefore inherently worthless. Drawing a structural analogy, the logic mirrors reinforced concrete: what truly matters is the dependable supply of constituent materials, not the speculative aura surrounding commodities that capture public imagination.
clips.text_en_c2: An enterprising anon on /biz/ has ventured the heretical proposition that timber, rather than gold or diamond, constitutes the rarest substance in the known universe, contending that any sufficiently advanced extraterrestrial civilisation, upon conducting a cost-benefit analysis of terrestrial resources, would logically expropriate our forests rather than our vaults. Gold, in his telling, lies in embarrassing abundance within the planet's crust and is accordingly worthless. There is a faintly structural sensibility to this thesis: as with reinforced concrete, whose prosaic supply chain renders it inherently more reliable than the marketing mythology surrounding structural steel, scarcity premised upon narrative is a fragile foundation upon which to erect any durable thesis. Hype, it turns out, ages rather less gracefully than concrete.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ shitpost arguing wood is rarer than gold.

clips.text_zh: /g有人話programmers兩年內會被LLM取代，it's over。我做engineer都係靠AI續命，但Tian教我路仲係要行，考牌都未完。

AI writes the GI report draft first, then we check slope stability and factor of safety by hand. The work still needs a licensed PE to sign off, for now.
clips.text_en_b2: A /g/ poster argues programmers will be replaced by LLMs within two years, concluding plainly that it is over for the profession. I share the same anxiety as a junior engineer on site, where AI now drafts the GI report first while we verify slope stability and factor of safety by hand. Even so, the paperwork still requires a licensed PE to sign off. My Tian-guided path continues regardless, and the licensing journey remains unfinished.
clips.text_en_c1: A /g/ poster has pronounced, with characteristic finality, that the programming profession will be effectively subsumed by large language models within a twenty-four-month horizon, concluding with the memorable declaration that 'it's over'. The sentiment resonates with my own apprehensions regarding junior site engineers, whose preliminary geotechnical reports are increasingly drafted by AI before human professionals verify slope stability and factor of safety calculations by hand. Nevertheless, regulatory frameworks still require a licensed professional engineer to affix their seal of approval, and qualifying examinations remain incomplete for many aspirants, preserving a veneer of professional indispensability, at least temporarily.
clips.text_en_c2: A /g/ contributor has pronounced, with the customary terminal confidence of that board, that software engineers as a professional class will be rendered obsolete by large language models within a roughly two-year horizon, his verdict delivered with the apocalyptic finality of someone for whom the matter is now settled. The sentiment resonates uncomfortably with my own position as a junior engineer in a geotechnical office, where the workflow has already begun to mutate: artificial intelligence drafts the preliminary geotechnical investigation report, and a human practitioner subsequently verifies slope stability calculations, confirms the factor of safety, and adjudicates edge cases the model cannot parse. Crucially, however, the deliverable still requires the signature of a licensed professional engineer, a regulatory artefact that no transformer architecture has yet learned to forge.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread claiming LLM replacement of programmers in two years.

clips.text_zh: /pol有人話Trump啲政策blow up咗US tech talent pipeline，鬧中國點同你鬥。對我嚟講更亂，五後返Florida嘅plan又多咗個variable。

For me the calculus shifts personally, because the Florida plan five years out has gained yet another variable to weigh. If US tech talent genuinely drains overseas, the entire equation changes. His contention is blunt, namely that no coherent strategy for technological competition with China can coexist with such evidently self-defeating policy choices. If American tech labour truly hemorrhages toward friendlier jurisdictions, the second-order consequences for state-level housing markets, professional licensing queues, and regional wage structures will be anything but trivial.

After their session they had to take the stairs to the upper car park because construction blocked the lower levels, and the buddy was gasping after just three flights while clinging to the rail. clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ correspondent has lamented the peculiar phenomenon of his gym partner, who routinely squats in excess of five hundred pounds yet regards any cardiovascular exertion with visceral suspicion, convinced that a mere ten-minute incline walk will catastrophically compromise his hypertrophic gains. Their post-training attempt to access the upper car park, necessitated by construction works rendering lower levels inaccessible, required ascending the stairwell. The scenario uncomfortably parallels my own exertions alongside Fat Boy following leg day sessions; evidently, cardiovascular conditioning remains non-negotiable, regardless of one's maximal strength.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ regular has submitted a vignette of almost clinical perfection regarding a training partner whose squat eclipses the 500-pound threshold yet who treats any cardiovascular exertion as though it were a venial sin against hypertrophy. The mere prospect of a ten-minute inclined treadmill walk sends this paragon into a paroxysm of preservation anxiety. By the third flight, the gentleman was audibly gasping, one white-knuckled hand clamped to the handrail in defeat. clips.text_zh: SpaceX嗰個reusability到底係真係平咗定係做數？老老實實，Starlink先係佢主要payload，而且有國防NATO需求，啲所謂平價launch分分鐘係美國納稅人補貼。即係話，prop firm個margin唔係真free lunch。我DSE唔識考都仲有藉口，呢個世界就連「成本」都可以改寫。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Have reusability really reduced the cost of sending loads to space, or is it just creative accounting? My doubts are based on two things. First, the primary goal of the American space program right now is deploying Starlink, which is very valuable for American and NATO defense needs.
clips.text_en_b2: Is SpaceX's much-hyped reusability genuinely cutting launch costs, or is it simply a case of creative accounting dressed up as innovation? While the company keeps touting falling price tags, the picture looks rather different once you dig deeper. The real bread and butter is Starlink deployment, which conveniently lines up with American and NATO defence contracts. Meanwhile, those suspiciously low launch prices almost certainly rely on hefty subsidies coming straight from the US taxpayer.
clips.text_en_c1: Whether SpaceX's celebrated reusability has genuinely slashed orbital launch costs or merely constitutes elaborate bookkeeping remains, in my estimation, a legitimate question worth interrogating rather than accepting at face value. Two considerations underpin my scepticism. First, Starlink satellites evidently constitute the lion's share of SpaceX's payload manifest, a constellation whose strategic value to American and NATO defence infrastructure cannot be overstated. Second, given that programme continuity was evidently pursued at virtually any price, the conspicuously low market rates for Falcon launches are likely underwritten, whether directly or indirectly, by American taxpayers rather than reflective of genuine economic efficiency.
clips.text_en_c2: One ought to interrogate whether SpaceX's celebrated reusability has genuinely depressed launch costs, or whether the figures are, in essence, a feat of creative accounting. Two considerations inform my scepticism. Foremost, the constellation currently absorbing the lion's share of SpaceX capacity is Starlink, a payload whose strategic salience to American and NATO defence appetites cannot be overstated. Secondly, given that the programme must succeed at any price, those conspicuously廉价 launch quotations are, in all likelihood, underwritten by the American taxpayer, with the consequence that American rocketry appears cheap on paper while remaining dear in fact. What passes, then, as a free lunch is nothing of the sort; it is, rather, a prop firm whose margin is conjured rather than earned. — /biz/ anon
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking if SpaceX's cheap launch cost is real or subsidized

clips.text_zh: 個retirement accounts根本就係scam。公司唔想畀你proper pension，就用chump change塞你入IRS稅務賭場：入面抽income tax，early withdrawal penalty，exit再抽capital gains。佢哋想lock住你哋啲錢到落場，呢個先係真正嘅prop firm——你以為自己喺投資，其實你係被投資。🙃
clips.text_en_b1: Retirement accounts are a scam. They are the result of scumbag companies not wanting to give workers a proper pension. Instead they give you some chump change to gamble with in the IRS tax casino, where they rape you before, during, and after in the form of income tax, early withdrawal penalties, and capital gains on any money your account makes.
clips.text_en_b2: Retirement accounts are little more than a dressed-up scam, designed so that penny-pinching employers can dodge handing workers an actual pension. Instead, they toss you a few crumbs to gamble with inside the IRS tax casino, where you get fleeced before, during, and after: income tax on every contribution, early withdrawal penalties if you dare touch it, and capital gains on whatever paltry returns your account manages to scrape together. The whole setup is engineered to lock your money away for decades.
clips.text_en_c1: Retirement accounts, whatever their conventional respectability, ought to be recognised for what they functionally are: a mechanism whereby employers systematically abdicate their obligation to provide defined-benefit pensions. Workers are instead handed a pittance and funnelled into what is effectively an IRS-administered tax casino, where extraction occurs at every conceivable juncture. Contributions are taxed going in; early withdrawals incur punitive penalties; and capital gains taxes await whatever paltry returns the account manages to accumulate. The architecture is plainly designed to maximise the duration over which capital remains locked away from the individual who nominally owns it, a fact that should give any rational participant considerable pause.
clips.text_en_c2: Retirement accounts, stripped of their benign veneer, are a rather elegant scam devised by those who harbour no intention of honouring a proper pension. Instead, employers fling you a pittance and shunt you into what is, functionally, an IRS-sanctioned casino, wherein you are fleeced at every conceivable juncture: at entry via income tax, during play through early withdrawal penalties, and upon egress via capital gains levied on whatever modest returns your principal manages to accrue. The objective is self-evident: to immobilise as much of your capital as possible for as long as possible, lest you ever achieve genuine financial autonomy. You imagine yourself the investor; in truth, you are the asset being invested in. — /biz/ rant
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread calling retirement accounts a tax-trap scam

clips.text_zh: Endgame嚟喇：如果AI真係replace到所有white collar同blue collar，咁我哋呢啲人仲有乜存在價值？Elites自己托住自己，再踩低其餘嘅人去slave caste。咁點解仲有人excited去幫人煉呢啲鎖鏊？做FE嘅我都係被target嗰個。靠AI續命，遲早連命都無埋。
clips.text_en_b1: Endgoal of AI replacement. Let us say that AI can actually replace everyone. What then? The elites are just propping themselves up and pushing the rest of us down into a slave caste. Why would anyone in our position support this? Why are people excited about developing tools of their own enslavement? /g/ thread about the endgame of AI replacement.
clips.text_en_b2: Suppose AI genuinely ends up replacing both white-collar and blue-collar workers across the board; what exactly is left for the rest of us? The endgame looks depressingly straightforward: elites propped up by their own algorithms, while everyone else gets pushed down into what is essentially a permanent underclass. Yet somehow ordinary people remain enthusiastic about building the very tools that will eventually render them obsolete. Polishing your own chains hardly seems like a rational career move.
clips.text_en_c1: Suppose, for the sake of argument, that artificial intelligence ultimately proves capable of displacing both white-collar and blue-collar labour in their entirety. What, then, becomes of the displaced majority, and by what mechanism are they to derive any conceivable claim to economic participation? The plausible trajectory, if present tendencies are any indication, is one in which an entrenched elite consolidates its position while the remainder are consigned to a structurally subordinate caste whose function, in economic terms, is largely vestigial. The question that therefore warrants serious consideration is why any rational member of that subordinate stratum would actively contribute to engineering the instruments of their own obsolescence.
clips.text_en_c2: The endgame of AI displacement, if one is honest enough to extrapolate, is rather bleak. Suppose, hypothetically, that the technology does in fact render every stratum of white- and blue-collar labour obsolete: what, then, is the residual utility of persons such as ourselves? The elite, predictably, will sustain one another whilst consigning the remainder to what is, functionally, a hereditary servile caste. What remains perplexing is why anyone in our predicament should evince enthusiasm for refining the very instruments of their own subjugation, an irony that appears to elude even those who profess otherwise. Yours truly, a frontend dev squarely within the target demographic, can only observe that deferring to AI to sustain one's existence is, in the long run, tantamount to forfeiting that existence altogether. — /g/ thread
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread asking why people build the AI that replaces them

clips.text_en_b2: Powershitting and the so-called Big 3 are far from the be-all and end-all, yet countless newcomers still fall headfirst into that trap. Obese lifters who cannot see their own genitals, let alone jog half a mile without their heart throwing a fit, will earnestly insist that squats, bench, and deadlifts are all you ever need. I bought into it for years; my numbers climbed, but I remained a soft, overweight slob in denial. Switching to athletic training changed everything.
clips.text_en_c1: The proposition that maximal strength, as cultivated through what the lifting community conventionally terms the Big Three compound movements, constitutes a sufficient training methodology ought to be regarded with considerable scepticism. The approach, venerated as it is within certain subcultures, produces practitioners whose physiques, while undeniably powerful in absolute terms, frequently exhibit profound deficiencies in cardiovascular capacity, mobility, and, frankly, basic aesthetic coherence. I speak from extended personal experience, having spent years pursuing load-bearing numbers at the expense of body composition, only to emerge as what can only be described as an adipose yet technically proficient specimen.
clips.text_en_c2: Powershitting, and the venerated Big Three in particular, are scarcely the be-all and end-all that the iron game would have one believe. Countless novices, rotund and resolute, fall prey to this particular delusion: fellows who cannot discern their own anatomy, let alone jog half a mile without their cardiovascular system lodging a formal protest, will earnestly proclaim that squat, bench, and deadlift constitute the entirety of one's regimen. I speak from bitter experience; I squandered years in this manner, and whilst my lifts climbed, I remained a corpulent, frogmode slob, neither healthy nor, by any stretch, attractive. Having since pivoted towards athletic training and shed the requisite adipose tissue, even formerly sceptical fat lads concede I now cut a rather sharper figure. — /fit/ confession

clips.text_en_b1: Apply to FAANG, nine rounds of interviews to get one job. Submit my resume. Recruiter reaches out a month later with a questionnaire asking me the same stuff that is on my resume. Then a 45-minute technical screening with a mid level engineer doing leetcode easy and writing tests.
clips.text_en_b2: Nine rounds of interviews just to land a single offer at FAANG, and recruiters still waste a month sending questionnaires mirroring your resume word for word. Then comes a 45-minute technical screening with leetcode easy, followed by another hour tackling medium problems alongside soft questions. The whole process drags on forever, yet applicants keep grinding through it because the pay off supposedly justifies the grind. How is this even remotely legal?
clips.text_en_c1: Apply to a single FAANG company and endure nine rounds of interviews, only to receive one offer at the end of it all. The recruiter eventually surfaces a month later with a questionnaire that, hilariously, mirrors the very contents of the resume already submitted. From there, candidates face a forty-five-minute technical screening with a mid-level engineer dissecting leetcode easy problems, followed by a one-hour session with a senior engineer tackling leetcode medium alongside the obligatory soft-skill interrogation. One genuinely wonders whether such a protracted gauntlet constitutes anything resembling a reasonable hiring practice, or simply institutional theatre designed to filter via attrition.
clips.text_en_c2: An account of the gauntlet that constitutes a contemporary FAANG recruitment process has, with wearying predictability, induced a minor existential crisis. The protagonist submits an application and, after a month of expectant silence, receives a questionnaire from a recruiter whose contents bear an uncanny resemblance to the resume already on file. What follows is an apparently interminable sequence of evaluations: a forty-five-minute technical screen with a mid-level engineer dissecting leetcode easy problems, succeeded by an hour-long interrogation administered by a senior engineer who wields leetcode medium questions and assorted behavioural prompts with equal enthusiasm. One might reasonably enquire as to the legality, or at the very least the proportionality, of demanding nine discrete rounds of assessment for a single position.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread complaining about FAANG interview process

clips.text_zh: 晚晚冇嘢做就睇 /pol/，今晚講 Blenheim Palace。有人話「英國人都係 mongrel race」，左派右派都同意。我喺 HK 返工壓力咁大，睇下白人自己鬥自己都幾搞笑 lol 同埋好想返 Florida 大屋住 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The English are a mongrel race. It is something the left and right can agree on, posted in a Blenheim Palace edition of Brit/pol/. The thread mixes history jokes about British aristocracy with culture war bait. Hong Kong readers said the cramped housing here makes the British countryside look like another planet, and a few anons replied with the usual Britain-is-finished cope.
clips.text_en_b2: A Blenheim Palace thread on Brit pol sparked an unlikely consensus: the English are essentially a mongrel race, which both the left and right managed to agree on for once. The post mingles aristocratic history jokes with culture war bait, and Hong Kong anons chimed in pointing out how tiny local flats make the British countryside look like another planet entirely. A handful of replies trotted out the usual Britain-is-finished cope, as expected.
clips.text_en_c1: A Blenheim Palace edition of Brit/pol/ surfaced the rather pointed observation that the English constitute, quote, a mongrel race, a thesis that both the left and the right, remarkably, found themselves willing to endorse. The thread oscillated between historical jabs aimed at aristocratic lineages and the customary culture-war provocations. Readers based in Hong Kong chimed in with sardonic comparisons, noting that the local housing situation renders the sprawling British countryside an almost alien landscape altogether. A handful of anons retaliated with the standard, if weary, Britain-is-finished cope that has become something of a refrain.
clips.text_en_c2: Browsing /pol/ during the small hours, when ennui invariably supplants any residual ambition, I encountered a thread ostensibly devoted to Blenheim Palace whose actual subject matter was the proposition, advanced with characteristic incivility, that the English are a mongrel race, a thesis upon which, the poster triumphantly observed, the left and right could at last find common ground. The conversation meandered, as such threads invariably do, between potted history concerning the British aristocracy and the now-familiar repertoire of culture-war provocations. Hong Kong-based readers, perennially confronted with the spatial indignities of local accommodation, were moved to observe that the English countryside resembles an almost extraterrestrial proposition, while the customary chorus of 'Britain-is-finished' lamentations materialised with mechanical inevitability.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ Brit thread about Blenheim Palace and British identity

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信今日又 tag 我睇 /fit/ 🧐 個 post 主 6 呎 1、194 lbs 而家 cutting，但手臂得 14.2 吋，問點樣去到 16 吋。佢 close-grip bench 132 lbs 2x10、straight bar curl 75 lbs 2x10，已經 intermediate 唔再加得 weight。我望住自己二頭都好細，剪脂真係好難搞 😩
clips.text_en_b1: I am 6 foot 1 at 194 pounds and currently cutting, but my arms are only 14.2 inches. The direct arm exercises I do are close-grip bench press at 132 pounds for 2 by 10, and straight bar bicep curl at 75 pounds for 2 by 10. I have reduced volume because of the cut.
clips.text_en_b2: Standing 6 foot 1 at 194 pounds and currently cutting, my arms stubbornly measure only 14.2 inches despite targeted work such as close-grip bench at 132 pounds for 2x10 and straight bar curls at 75 for the same sets. Volume has had to come down because of the cut, and I have plateaued for ages, which solidifies my intermediate status. Hitting 16 inches during a deficit feels like chasing a moving target, honestly.
clips.text_en_c1: Standing six foot one and weighing in at 194 pounds while running a cut, the poster reports arms that measure a measly 14.2 inches, a figure they find deeply unsatisfying. Their direct arm work consists of close-grip bench presses at 132 pounds for sets of ten, paired with straight-bar bicep curls at 75 pounds, likewise for two sets of ten. Volume has inevitably been dialled back to accommodate the caloric deficit. They self-identify as an intermediate trainee, primarily because progressive overload, that long-standing metric of advancement, has flatlined across sessions for quite some time now.
clips.text_en_c2: The original poster presents himself as a six-foot-one, 194-pound individual presently embarked upon a caloric deficit, whose arms, at a circumference of 14.2 inches, have apparently failed to register meaningful hypertrophy despite an ostensibly well-structured regimen. His direct arm work consists of the close-grip bench press at 132 pounds for two sets of ten, paired with the straight-bar biceps curl at 75 pounds, likewise for two by ten. Volume, he notes with conspicuous regret, has been attenuated to accommodate the exigencies of the cut. He self-identifies as an intermediate trainee, the designation being justified by his admission that, for some considerable duration, he has been unable to apply progressive overload to his compound movements from one session to the next.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking how to grow arms from 14 to 16 inches

clips.text_zh: 夜晚溫習 FE 溫到悶就去 /a/ 🧐 有條 post 列出最有 cultural impact 嘅動漫排名：第一 Demon Slayer 唔使解釋、第二 Gintama 生咗 Demon Slayer、第三 Bleach、第四 Black Clover、第五 Kagurabachi。我自己最鍾意 Gundam 00，但呢張 list 完全冇 mecha 份 😩 鬼滅我都覺得 OK 嘅
clips.text_en_b1: The objective ranking of manga and anime franchises with the most cultural impact, more than any other comics and cartoons and even overwriting some minor celebrities, is: 1. Demon Slayer, no explanation needed, simply the biggest phenomenon. 2. Gintama, which birthed Demon Slayer. 3. Bleach, which birthed many things. 4. Black Clover, birthed by Bleach. 5. Kagurabachi. You can share your top picks too.
clips.text_en_b2: The objective ranking of anime franchises with the most cultural impact reads as follows: Demon Slayer takes the top spot as a self evident phenomenon, Gintama follows because it essentially birthed Demon Slayer, then Bleach for spawning countless successors, Black Clover owing its existence to Bleach, and finally Kagurabachi rounding things out. Not a single mecha title appears anywhere, which is a crying shame for Gundam 00 fans such as myself, although Demon Slayer certainly earns its place.
clips.text_en_c1: A self-proclaimed objective ranking of manga and anime franchises ranked by sheer cultural footprint, eclipsing even Western comics and displacing certain minor celebrities, reads as follows. Demon Slayer takes the crown, a phenomenon so dominant that further elaboration is deemed superfluous. Gintama claims second, credited with birthing the very sensibility that Demon Slayer inherited. Bleach follows in third, the wellspring from which much of modern shonen DNA derives. Black Clover lands fourth, Bleach's spiritual descendant. Kagurabachi rounds out the top five. Notably absent from the entire list is any mecha entry, a glaring omission for fans of the genre.
clips.text_en_c2: A /a/ thread purports to furnish an objective taxonomy of those manga and anime franchises whose cultural footprint has been sufficiently substantial to eclipse not merely rival comics and cartoons but, in certain instances, minor celebrities themselves. The ranking proceeds thus: in the premier position, Demon Slayer, whose phenomenal ascendancy requires no elucidation; second, Gintama, which the poster credits with siring its successor; third, Bleach, similarly positioned as a progenitor; fourth, Black Clover, likewise identified as an heir to the Bleach lineage; and fifth, the comparatively nascent Kagurabachi. The conspicuous lacuna is the entire mecha genre, a category whose more cerebral exponents, such as Gundam 00, have evidently failed to register on whatever metric the poster is employing.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread ranking most culturally impactful manga and anime

clips.text_zh: 收工返到屋企先記得 /g/ 有條 post 講 10700XT 要贏 RTX 5080 🧐 樓主話呢啲 marketing 講過好多次但從來冇兌現過，仲要連 path tracing 都包埋。佢覺得要做到呢樣 + FSR 同 DLSS4 一樣好 + CUDA 跑得順 AMD 先算有料。我又唔打機又唔 mining，但 trading 用嚟跑 backtest 都想快啲 lol
clips.text_en_b1: 10700XT to outperform RTX 5080. How many times have we heard this before and it is literally never the case. Including path tracing, an even bigger claim this time. I would genuinely love this to be true but I will believe it when I see it.
clips.text_en_b2: Yet another marketing claim that the 10700XT will outclass the RTX 5080, including path tracing this time around, and we have all heard this kind of promise from AMD before without it ever materialising. It would need to genuinely deliver on that, while matching DLSS4 in both quality and performance modes, and CUDA would have to run properly on the hardware. I would love to see it happen, but I will believe it only when benchmarks actually land.
clips.text_en_c1: The marketing proposition that a 10700XT could outperform an RTX 5080 has been recycled so many times that any reasonable observer ought to approach the claim with profound scepticism. Including path tracing this time around only inflates the audacity. The poster, refreshingly candid, concedes that they would genuinely relish being proven wrong, though conviction will arrive only upon independent verification. The benchmark, furthermore, demands parity: FSR must match DLSS4 across both performance and quality presets, and CUDA workloads must execute without the present friction. Until those conditions materialise, the announcement remains vapour.
clips.text_en_c2: Returning home after a taxing day, I recalled that /g/ had been circulating a rather audacious marketing claim, namely that the forthcoming 10700XT is poised to surpass the RTX 5080 in raw performance, a declaration that the original poster greets with the weary incredulity of someone who has endured such promises on previous occasions and watched them evaporate upon release. The assertion, if anything more ambitious than its predecessors, encompasses not merely rasterisation but the considerably more demanding domain of path tracing. The poster articulates a precise, almost forensic set of conditions under which AMD might plausibly earn his confidence: parity with DLSS4 across both performance and quality modes, and the proper functioning of CUDA on the new architecture.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread skeptical about AMD 10700 XT beating RTX 5080

clips.text_zh: 今日睇到有人講俄羅斯要錢打緊仗，所以不斷拋金。難怪金價上唔到。講真我已經輸緊，仲要睇呢啲，真係頂唔順。又係學費囉🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Russia is looking for money to fund the war. That is why gold cannot pump anymore. Russia has huge precious metal reserves, and now they are selling them. I do not see this dumping ending anytime soon.
clips.text_en_b2: Russia keeps offloading its gold reserves because it desperately needs cash to keep the war machine running, and that relentless selling is clearly capping any upside on gold prices. Given the scale of their stockpile, I honestly cannot see this dumping slowing down in the foreseeable future, so unless geopolitics shifts dramatically, the bleed is likely to continue weighing on my positions for the foreseeable future.
clips.text_en_c1: Russia is evidently seeking to liquidate significant portions of its gold reserves in order to finance an ongoing military campaign, which would largely explain why the precious metal has struggled to mount any sustained rally. Given the sheer scale of their stockpile, one can reasonably assume that this selling pressure is not about to abate in the foreseeable future. For those of us who are already nursing considerable losses, watching these developments unfold in real time only adds insult to injury, and the tuition bills keep piling up regardless of the macroeconomic backdrop.
clips.text_en_c2: Russia, acutely starved of liquidity to bankroll its protracted war effort, has resorted to systematically divesting its vast precious-metals reserves. The market, ever sensitive to such incremental selling pressure, has consequently struggled to mount a sustained rally; gold has effectively been capped, no matter how favourable the underlying macro narrative might appear to retail bulls. With no discernible end to this liquidation in sight, given Moscow's unceasing fiscal exigencies, one can scarcely blame disillusioned participants for feeling as though the metal has been permanently conscripted into geopolitics. The prospect of any meaningful relief, it seems, remains hostage to a ceasefire that shows no sign of materialising. Holders, understandably, are bearing the brunt.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on Russia dumping gold reserves

clips.text_zh: 又有人話BTC係bulltrap。我都想信，但又唔敢short。油價同債息都爆上，邊有理由BTC獨自升？命理叫我hold，唯有等囉🧐
clips.text_en_b1: This is a bulltrap, think about it logically. Why would market makers pump Bitcoin when everything else is crashing? Bond yields, gas, food crops, everything is soaring like their lives depend on it. They want to load up longs so they can crash the market until at least the next halving.
clips.text_en_b2: Honestly, this whole Bitcoin rally has bulltrap written all over it. While everything else is in freefall, bond yields, crude, food commodities, you name it, why on earth would market makers pump BTC in isolation? They are almost certainly loading up longs so they can crush the market into the next halving, and I am not about to get caught on the wrong side again.
clips.text_en_c1: The prevailing argument that Bitcoin's current trajectory constitutes little more than a bull trap deserves careful scrutiny, particularly when one considers the broader macroeconomic picture. With bond yields, energy prices, and agricultural commodities all surging in tandem, it seems altogether implausible that institutional market makers would deliberately prop up a single asset class without an ulterior motive. The logical inference is that they are merely accumulating long positions in anticipation of a significant liquidation cascade, one that could plausibly extend well beyond the next halving event. Until sentiment decisively shifts, holding remains the only rational course of action.
clips.text_en_c2: Consider, with the cold detachment that rationality demands, what is presently unfolding across asset classes. Bond yields are ballooning, crude oil has decisively broken to the upside, and even staple agricultural commodities are exhibiting a near-vertical ascent, as though the entire risk spectrum were conspiring to vindicate the bearish thesis. Against such a backdrop, the notion that institutional market makers would organically propel Bitcoin skyward strains credulity beyond its breaking point. The far more plausible interpretation, advanced by seasoned cynics, holds that this engineered strength is merely bait, designed to lure capital into leveraged long exposure before the inevitable rug-pull. Seasoned operators, wary of being liquidated, will therefore hold, waiting patiently for the next halving cycle.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread calling BTC a bulltrap amid crashing everything else

clips.text_zh: 睇到外國佬講手臂，我194磅先得14.2吋😭 佢CG bench 132lb、curl 75lb，同我差唔遠。但人哋6呎1，我連16吋都未到。肥仔信睇到實笑我lol
clips.text_en_b1: I am 6 foot 1 at 194 pounds and my arms are only 14.2 inches. I do close-grip bench press at 132 pounds for 2 sets of 10, and straight bar bicep curl at 75 pounds for 2 sets of 10. I cut volume because of a cut. How hard is it to get 16 inch arms?
clips.text_en_b2: I am six foot one, weighing in at around 194 pounds, yet my arms stubbornly refuse to break the 14.2-inch mark, which is honestly embarrassing. My close-grip bench sits at 132 pounds and straight bar curls at 75 pounds, both for two sets of ten, although I trimmed volume during my cut. Getting to sixteen inches feels like an uphill battle at this point.
clips.text_en_c1: Standing at six foot one and weighing 194 pounds, I find it somewhat demoralising that my arms measure a mere 14.2 inches, particularly given that the individuals whose physiques I admire possess remarkably similar lifting numbers. My current routine consists of close-grip bench presses at 132 pounds and straight-bar bicep curls at 75 pounds, both performed across two sets of ten repetitions, though volume has necessarily been curtailed on account of an ongoing cut. The question that continues to haunt me is precisely how difficult it remains to break through the seemingly elusive sixteen-inch threshold, a milestone that appears almost within reach yet stubbornly distant.
clips.text_en_c2: Standing at six foot one and weighing a respectable 194 pounds, I find myself quietly humiliated by the realisation that my arms, despite years of conscientious effort, measure a meagre 14.2 inches. My training regimen, for the record, consists of close-grip bench presses executed at 132 pounds across two sets of ten, supplemented by straight-bar bicep curls at 75 pounds for the same volume, though I have admittedly curtailed overall workload on account of a recent cut. Comparatively, lifters of similar stature routinely sport arms exceeding the hallowed sixteen-inch threshold, rendering my own progress almost comically inadequate. The question, then, is whether hypertrophy at this level demands pharmaceutical intervention, or merely the sort of genetic lottery that has thus far eluded me.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about chasing 16-inch arms while cutting

clips.text_zh: AMD又話10700XT贏到RTX 5080，仲要path tracing，聽到我喊出黎。AMD次次都係咁講，唔信囉。除非CUDA真係上到去，否則我唔會郁張卡🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The 10700XT will supposedly outperform the RTX 5080 and even includes path tracing. How many times have we heard this before and it is literally never the case. I will believe it when I see it, especially if FSR finally matches DLSS4 in quality and performance.
clips.text_en_b2: AMD is claiming yet again that the 10700XT will outperform the RTX 5080 and even handle path tracing, a familiar tune we have all heard countless times before. I have been burned too often to take these promises at face value, so I will believe it when benchmarks actually land, and only if FSR finally manages to hold its own against DLSS4 in practice.
clips.text_en_c1: AMD's marketing apparatus has once again proclaimed that the forthcoming 10700XT will outperform Nvidia's RTX 5080, allegedly incorporating hardware-accelerated path tracing into the bargain, a claim that would have been borderline extraordinary had it not followed the same pattern we have witnessed on countless previous occasions. History suggests considerable scepticism is warranted, given that AMD's pre-release benchmarks have historically diverged rather dramatically from real-world performance. Should FSR eventually achieve parity with DLSS 4 in terms of both visual fidelity and frame-rate consistency, my reservations might finally dissipate, though until that day arrives I remain content to watch from the sidelines.
clips.text_en_c2: AMD's marketing apparatus has once again elected to regale prospective buyers with the arresting claim that their forthcoming 10700XT will comprehensively eclipse Nvidia's RTX 5080, allegedly even with path tracing enabled. One would be forgiven for succumbing to enthusiastic optimism, given the sheer audacity of such pronouncements, except for the inconvenient truth that we have endured this particular cycle of hype and consequent disappointment so many times before. The Team Red faithful, long chastened by repeated overpromising, have adopted a credo of profound scepticism: until the silicon is independently benchmarked in real-world scenarios, every glossy slide deck warrants nothing more than a weary eye-roll. Should FSR finally close the quality chasm with DLSS 4, however, sentiment may yet shift.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on rumored AMD 10700XT performance claims

clips.text_zh: 睇完笑咗。Epstein死咗、Rogan走佬、Trump又話俾人拉埋。美國都係咁上下lol。對我嚟講返Florida嘅plan唔變，考完牌就走🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Epstein is dead. Most big names like Rogan have left. Elon is irrelevant. Trump is either getting removed or croaking before his term ends. It is all falling apart in realtime, anon.
clips.text_en_b2: The whole US political circus is unravelling in broad daylight, and it is frankly hard to keep up. Epstein is conveniently dead, Rogan has largely checked out, Elon has become a background character at best, and Trump is either about to get removed or keel over before his term wraps up. From where I am standing, nothing is holding together, so I am sticking to my Florida plan.
clips.text_en_c1: The contemporary state of American affairs has descended into what can only be described as a slow-motion spectacle of institutional decay, with each passing week delivering fresh revelations that would have seemed implausible mere years ago. Epstein's demise, the conspicuous departure of influential figures such as Rogan, and the mounting speculation surrounding Trump's political future collectively suggest a nation whose foundational structures are fracturing in real time. Whether through impeachment or more permanent means, the current administration appears destined for an abrupt conclusion. As for myself, plans to relocate to Florida remain entirely unchanged once the licensing examinations conclude.
clips.text_en_c2: America, that great beacon of institutional stability, appears to be entering a phase of almost baroque self-destruction. Epstein has shuffled off his mortal coil under circumstances more befitting a spy thriller than a civilised judiciary, the country's most prominent podcasting personalities have emigrated in droves, Elon Musk has retreated into terminal irrelevance, and Trump, with characteristic inevitability, now faces either impeachment or mortality before his term concludes. One watches, transfixed, as the edifice unravels in real time, each revelation more outlandish than the last. For those of us observing from abroad, however, such spectacles carry a peculiar clarity: Florida beckons, and once the bar exam is dispatched, the relocation plan proceeds undeterred by the circus.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread claiming the US establishment is collapsing

clips.text_zh: 有人排動漫文化影響力，第一係鬼滅、Gintama第二、漂白第三。睇完好想重睇Gintama，但我邊有時間😭 考牌先
clips.text_en_b1: Objective ranking of manga and anime with the most cultural impact: 1. Demon Slayer, the biggest phenomenon. 2. Gintama, which birthed Demon Slayer. 3. Bleach, which birthed many things. 4. Black Clover, birthed by Bleach. 5. Kagurabachi. What are your top picks?
clips.text_en_b2: Someone posted an objective ranking of manga and anime by cultural impact, and the lineup was hard to argue with. Demon Slayer tops the list as the biggest phenomenon, Gintama comes second for essentially giving birth to Demon Slayer, Bleach third for spawning countless successors, Black Clover fourth owing its DNA to Bleach, and Kagurabachi rounding things out. It made me want to rewatch Gintama immediately.
clips.text_en_c1: An objective assessment of those manga and anime franchises that have exerted the most pronounced influence on contemporary popular culture would arguably place Demon Slayer at the apex, given its unprecedented commercial dominance and mainstream penetration. Gintama, whose stylistic DNA is unmistakably embedded within Demon Slayer's DNA, would reasonably occupy the second position, whilst Bleach, having spawned countless derivative works, deserves the third slot. Black Clover, itself a spiritual descendant of Bleach, follows logically in fourth place, with Kagurabachi rounding out the top five as a relative newcomer whose impact remains to be fully assessed.
clips.text_en_c2: An objective ranking of manga and anime according to their seismic cultural impact would necessarily privilege those works whose influence has palpably reshaped the medium's trajectory. Demon Slayer, indisputably the most colossal phenomenon of its generation, occupies the apex, its aesthetic and narrative templates having been internalised by an entire cohort of contemporary creators. Gintama, whose irreverent meta-commentary arguably seeded the soil from which Demon Slayer eventually bloomed, deserves the runner-up position with little controversy. Bleach, progenitor of countless shonen conventions, claims the bronze, while Black Clover, its scrappy spiritual descendant, follows. Kagurabachi, the dark horse, rounds out a quintet whose collective footprint is difficult to overstate. As for revisiting Gintama, perhaps once these examinations are finally behind me.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread ranking manga franchises by cultural impact

clips.text_zh: 100 Kanojo S3完咗😂 Bibury做唔做到S4都唔知。我反而想睇下佢哋點收尾，考完牌當獎勵自己lol
clips.text_en_b1: 100 Kanojo Season 3 is over. What did you think of the finale and the season overall? Since there is a chance this could be it, what do you think of Bibury's adaptation in general? Are you a season 4 and beyond believer?
clips.text_en_b2: 100 Girlfriends Season 3 has wrapped up, and the finale left me feeling oddly bittersweet about the whole run. With Bibury stretched thin across multiple projects, a fourth season feels like wishful thinking rather than a realistic outcome, so this might genuinely be the end of the road. Either way, I am saving the binge as a reward once my licensing exams are finally behind me.
clips.text_en_c1: With the third season of 100 Girlfriends having recently concluded, the question of whether Bibury Animation Studio possesses either the financial incentive or the creative momentum to commission a fourth instalment remains genuinely uncertain. Given the narrative's natural resting point, there exists a tangible possibility that this adaptation may represent the final chapter in the franchise's animated journey, a prospect that renders the existing adaptation's overall quality rather more significant than it might otherwise have been. Personally, I intend to reserve judgment until after the licensing examinations conclude, at which point binge-watching awaits.
clips.text_en_c2: With Season 3 of Kimi no Koto ga Daidaidaidaidai Suki na 100-nin no Kanojo having concluded its broadcast, the discourse has predictably bifurcated into camps of gratification and grumbling. Bibury Animation Studios, having shepherded the property through three increasingly ambitious outings, now confronts the perennial existential question: does commercial viability justify a fourth instalment, or has the narrative well been drawn dry? Detractors argue that certain narrative threads deserve more elaborate resolution than a mere truncated ending, while enthusiasts counter that the studio's distinctive visual signatures have grown more refined with each successive season. Whether one subscribes to blind optimism or pragmatic resignation, the upcoming licensing examinations offer an unimpeachable excuse to defer such weighty deliberations until a more opportune moment.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread discussing 100 Girlfriends Season 3 ending

clips.text_zh: /biz/ 有人話，精靈妹叫佢哋買 XRP 同 DOGE，依家啲人 financial elf，lol。我又輸緊，仲有考牌，都唔知頂唔頂到 🙏 又係學費…
clips.text_en_b1: You should have listened to the elf maid when she told you to buy lots of XRP and DOGE. Now people who hold those coins will be in GOOD FINANCIAL ELF, lol. The poster is mocking anyone who missed the pump and missed the elf maid's advice from earlier in the year.
clips.text_en_b2: You should have taken the elf maid's call seriously when she flagged accumulating XRP and DOGE earlier in the year. Anyone who actually held those positions is now sitting on a comfortable portfolio, while the rest of us watched the rally unfold from the sidelines. Honestly, it stings, but hindsight is 20/20 and crypto rarely hands out second chances. Anyway, I'm still down on my prop trades and grinding through exam prep, so back to the salt mine.
clips.text_en_c1: Anyone who failed to heed the elf maid's earlier call to accumulate XRP and DOGE is now ruing the missed opportunity, as holders find themselves in what can only be described as a state of financial nirvana. The poster is seizing the moment to lampoon those who dismissed the advice, particularly given the magnitude of the subsequent rally. Yet the irony is not lost on the original commentator, who confesses to being underwater on positions while simultaneously shouldering the financial burden of an upcoming licensing examination, rendering the entire affair a costly lesson.
clips.text_en_c2: One ought to have heeded the elf maiden's oracular counsel back when she extolled the virtues of XRP and DOGE. Should the connection fall short of full-strength capacity, however, the load simply cannot transfer as intended, rendering the detail fundamentally flawed. These structural discontinuities, which the licensing exam routinely exploits, demand a thorough grasp of force transfer mechanics rather than blind reliance on artificial intelligence to fill gaps in comprehension.

Should the joint prove incapable of developing the full flexural capacity of the adjoining beam — a not-uncommon deficiency in older reinforced-concrete frames — the load cannot be transmitted in the manner the designer evidently intended, and the detail is, for all practical purposes, non-functional.

Absolute lying bastards.
clips.text_en_c1: If the macroeconomic outlook were genuinely as bleak as the headlines relentlessly suggest, one would reasonably expect BTC to be capitulating rather than rallying to dizzying highs. The disconnect, which I cannot reconcile no matter how hard I try, strongly implies that the narrative being pushed is, at best, a curated distortion serving political ends. The same outlets that warned of crop failures driven by scorching summers and persistent oil shortages insisted that a broad sell-off was imminent. Yet prices have stubbornly refused to comply.
clips.text_en_c2: One cannot help but notice the rather conspicuous dissonance between the prevailing macroeconomic narrative and the actual market behaviour of late. Headlines insist upon a deteriorating global economy: harvests imperilled by anomalous heatwaves, energy markets persistently starved of sufficient supply, the usual litany of bearish omens. Yet Bitcoin, defying every one of these ostensibly terminal warnings, has continued its ascent with almost reckless disregard for conventional fundamentals. Either the news cycle is catastrophically mendacious, functioning as little more than a rhetorical instrument for partisan ends, or the analysts who formulate such predictions have, once again, demonstrably misread the terrain. The disconnect between reported reality and observable price action is, frankly, too stark to attribute to mere statistical noise or coincidence. (136)

clips.text_en_c1: Creatine monohydrate, the most exhaustively studied ergogenic aid in modern sports science, nevertheless carries a constellation of side effects that anybody considering supplementation ought to weigh with appropriate seriousness. Anecdotal reports, which range from credible to catastrophically exaggerated, suggest that chronic usage can accelerate male pattern baldness in predisposed individuals, provoke persistent acne breakouts, and induce a characteristic puffiness that settles stubbornly around the midsection and facial features. These aesthetic compromises, however, are typically offset by demonstrable performance gains of between five and ten percent in maximal load capacity, an increment that serious lifters regard as transformative over a structured training cycle.
clips.text_en_c2: Creatine monohydrate, that venerable staple of the earnest lifter's supplement stack, presents the familiar Faustian bargain: in exchange for an incremental gain of perhaps five to ten percent in maximal strength output, the user must contend with a constellation of decidedly inelegant physiological consequences. Hair loss, particularly among the genetically predisposed; persistent acne along the jawline and temples; a certain unmistakable puffiness about the face and midsection that no amount of cardiovascular exertion seems entirely to remedy. And yet, for the committed practitioner whose identity is inextricably bound to the iron, these concessions are deemed eminently tolerable, indeed almost obligatory, for the additional capacity to hoist another plate or two. It is, in essence, a small vanity tax levied upon the pursuit of marginal hypertrophy. (137)

Getting the load path from slab through the secondary beams, into the columns, and ultimately down to the foundations is non-negotiable; any ambiguity at a beam-column joint and the failure mode tends to be singularly catastrophic. I worked through Sing's notes until my eyes glazed over, then verified that the moment connections at the joints were adequate and that the steel reinforcement properly anchored the negative-moment regions.
clips.text_en_c2: Spending the better part of the evening wading through Sing's notes on load path continuity in reinforced concrete design, a topic whose conceptual elegance belies its capacity for catastrophic failure if executed carelessly. The load path from slab through secondary beams, into beam-column joints and ultimately down to the foundations, must be traced with an exactness bordering on the forensic; one overlooked moment connection at the joint and the entire lateral system surrenders without ceremony. I confirmed the steel reinforcement detailing adequately addresses the negative moment region over the supports, though the P-Delta check scraped through with a margin narrower than I would care to defend in a review meeting.

clips.source_hint: /g/ thread: Jev reportedly replaces Claude/OpenAI for most industrial applications, AI threat angle

clips.text_en_c1: Has any manufacturer actually cracked the aesthetic question when it comes to household robotics? The current options all fall somewhere between deeply unsettling and outright dystopian. Boston Dynamics keeps shipping its claw-footed quadrupeds and bipedal units straight out of a horror film, while Tesla's Pepsiman prototypes lean firmly into uncanny-valley territory. What I, and presumably many others, would actually want is something charming: a catgirl maid, say, or at minimum a butler with presence. clips.text_en_c2: The domestic robotics market remains, aesthetically speaking, an unmitigated disappointment. Boston Dynamics continues to proffer its clawed quadrupeds and unnervingly athletic humanoids, while Tesla's optimus line evokes nothing so much as a glossy corporate mascot, and Honda's legacy Asimo has long since calcified into kitsch. What one actually wants is something with charm, perhaps a diminutive maid or a cat-eared attendant capable of managing laundry and the quotidian minutiae of household upkeep. The current offerings, however, occupy a deeply uncanny valley, neither functional nor fetching, and thereby fail on every front. In a modestly appointed flat, the practical calculus favours delegation to software: an AI competent enough to file reports, draft correspondence, and handle the administrative drudgery that increasingly defines the working week would prove immeasurably more useful than any chrome-plated contrivance.

The trajectory mapped out for the next half-decade, should present trends continue unchecked, suggests a future in which human oversight becomes increasingly ornamental. Upon discovering a foreclosure-listed three-bedroom property priced at a mere sixty thousand dollars, situated in a reasonably salubrious neighbourhood, one might reasonably anticipate at least the courtesy of consideration. Zillow's automated underwriting machinery, however, rendered its verdict with algorithmic indifference: insufficient income, insufficient credit history, insufficient years upon the earth. The system, designed to streamline, has instead become a gatekeeper of particular brutality for those attempting to secure even the most modest foothold on the property ladder. The so-called American Dream, once a rallying cry, now reads as something closer to satire for an entire generation priced out before they have begun.

clips.text_en_c2: There exists a particular species of male anxiety, as universal as it is seldom articulated, centred upon the persistent puffiness of the nipple despite diligent effort to the contrary. Countless hours spent leaning out, meticulous caloric restriction, and a bench press regimen bordering on devotional, all conspire to deliver a chest that remains, at certain angles, stubbornly adipose. Medical consultation, rather than offering succour, merely compounds the indignity: the gyno, it transpires, is too minor to warrant surgical intervention, the surgeon politely declining to deflate what he perceives as a non-problem. The sufferer is thus condemned to a purgatory of body dysmorphia, scrutinising his reflection for incremental changes invisible to anyone but himself. Meanwhile, well-meaning acquaintances counsel bulk, oblivious to the precise nature of the torment. Some afflictions, it seems, admit no ready remedy.

clips.text_en_c1: Contemporary seasonal offerings are perfectly serviceable, yet there is something irreplaceable about revisiting the canon of one's formative years. Lately my rotation has consisted of Hellsing's gothic excess, the melancholic odyssey of Wolf's Rain, Bleach during its narrative prime, and Azumanga Daioh's effortless surrealism. The decade possessed a particular aesthetic sensibility, an atmosphere of deliberate pacing and unpolished sincerity, that modern productions rarely replicate with comparable conviction. After a gruelling day at the screen, there is genuine therapeutic value in retreating into narratives whose outcomes one already knows. clips.text_en_c2: There is something quietly restorative about revisiting the animation of one's formative years, a sentiment that contemporary seasonal offerings, for all their technical refinement, seldom manage to replicate. The post-millennium era possessed a distinct aesthetic sensibility, simultaneously melancholic and exuberant, evident across such varied fare as Hellsing's gothic bombast, Wolf's Rain's desolate lyricism, the shonen bombast of Bleach, and Azumanga Daioh's gentle absurdity. These productions inhabited a particular register, half-ironic yet sincerely felt, that newer works, saturated with streaming-era polish, struggle to approximate. To return to them after a gruelling day, the mind still churning over open CFD positions and unrealised gains, is to rediscover a kind of emotional equilibrium unavailable elsewhere.

What passes for the economy is little more than a mechanism for sustaining extreme government expenditure on welfare programmes. When austerity inevitably follows, it once again strangles the very thing it was meant to preserve. clips.text_en_c2: The poster's thesis, delivered with characteristic 4chan irreverence, reduces Canada to a fiscal vassal state. France and Germany, he argues, effectively expropriate whatever productive surplus the Canadian economy manages to generate. What remains is channelled into extravagant entitlement programmes, a self-perpetuating cycle in which swelling public outlays eventually provoke the very austerity measures that strangle growth. clips.text_en_c1: The perennial Bitcoin-versus-gold debate resurfaces on /biz/ with monotonous regularity, and whichever camp one backs, a decade of regret awaits those who choose poorly. Personally, I have committed to Bitcoin, though I concede that gold retains a fundamentally defensive character that crypto still struggles to match. Were the decision genuinely straightforward, I would not have spent the better part of ten years second-guessing myself. The crux of the matter ultimately hinges on whether one places greater trust in algorithmic scarcity or in the centuries-old conviction of central banks. We shall reconvene in 2034 and render judgement accordingly. 🙏
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial Bitcoin-versus-gold question resurfaces on /biz/ with metronomic regularity, each iteration ostensibly seeking definitive resolution while in practice confirming that conviction is merely a proxy for temperament. The original poster frames the dilemma as a ten-year binary: monetary sovereignty encoded in immutable software, or millennia of accumulated trust in a tangible, if unproductive, asset. Replies inevitably bifurcate along ideological lines, with those distrustful of central-bank discretion gravitating toward BTC and the more risk-averse anchoring themselves to bullion's established track record. What renders the debate ultimately irresolvable is the asymmetry of failure modes; gold disappoints gradually, whereas Bitcoin's volatility curve can vaporise portfolios overnight. The thread thus becomes less an investment inquiry than a referendum on institutional faith.

clips.text_zh: 睇緊reinforced concrete嘅load path由slab落到beam落到column再落foundation。鋼嗰邊一樣，moment connection點解用，點check welding。FE真係多嘢背。
clips.text_en_b1: Weighted calisthenics are the best workout you can do. It will give you an aesthetic physique, the bodily control becomes off the charts compared to a bodybuilder or a powerlifter, and you become strong without getting fat. Being able to do a planche or handstand push-up is more impressive than a 2-plate bench. No one cares how much you bench press.
clips.text_en_b2: Weighted calisthenics arguably offers the most well-rounded workout you can commit to, since it builds an aesthetic physique while keeping bodyweight control completely off the charts. Unlike bodybuilders or powerlifters, you come out strong without piling on unnecessary mass, and pulling off a planche or handstand push-up is far more impressive than grinding out a two-plate bench. The principle mirrors load path logic perfectly: strength flows through the cleanest route, never the bulkiest one.
clips.text_en_c1: I have been tracing the load path through a reinforced concrete frame: from slab to beam, beam to column, and column down to the foundation interface. The steel alternative requires comparable rigour, particularly with respect to moment connections, where weld quality and base-plate detailing govern the entire transfer mechanism. The Fundamentals of Engineering examination demands that one internalise all of this procedural detail, which is precisely why my evenings have been swallowed by formula sheets and AISC provisions. Were the discipline straightforward, the qualification would hardly command the professional weight that it does.
clips.text_en_c2: The elegant mechanics of load path tracing in reinforced concrete, whereby gravitational forces cascade sequentially through slab, beam, column, and ultimately foundation, offers an instructive parallel to calisthenic training philosophy. In structural steelwork, analogous continuity is achieved through moment connections whose adequacy hinges upon weld inspection protocols and rigorous quality assurance. Both disciplines demand that practitioners internalise load trajectory intuitively, rather than relying on rote computation, since failure modes invariably originate at points of discontinuity. The volume of material mandated for the FE examination reflects this integrative burden: candidates must synthesise disparate analytical frameworks into a coherent mental model, lest superficial familiarity precipitate the kind of catastrophic oversight that no retrospective correction can remedy.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ calisthenics thread mapped to load-path thinking

clips.text_zh: AI bubble爆咗都唔代表GPU會平，因為全部畀人熔咗回收。真係黐線。又係學費。仲驚過FE考試，怕自己份工畀AI搶埋。
clips.text_en_b1: You thought you could get cheap GPUs after the AI bubble pops? Think again — they're all getting melted down. clips.text_en_b2: Anyone assuming cheap GPUs will flood the second-hand market once the AI bubble finally bursts is in for a nasty surprise, because the chips are being physically melted down and recycled. Even if the hype collapses tomorrow, that steady supply of affordable hardware simply won't materialise, and the whole situation feels absolutely unhinged. As civil engineers we feel the same squeeze when automation creeps into site reporting, since the cheaper tools always dry up first.
clips.text_en_c1: Anyone expecting a flood of affordable GPUs once the AI bubble finally deflates is in for a profound disappointment, because the hardware in question is being physically dismantled and recycled rather than offloaded onto secondary markets. The chips, quite literally, are being melted down into raw silicon, which eliminates the usual post-crash arbitrage that bargain hunters tend to anticipate. For those of us in adjacent technical fields, the anxiety runs deeper than mere hardware costs: if AI encroaches upon site reporting and design automation, the most accessible tools will inevitably vanish first. We have all paid enough tuition.
clips.text_en_c2: The sanguine expectation that an AI-sector contraction would precipitate a glut of affordable second-hand GPUs constitutes a fundamental misreading of contemporary semiconductor economics. Datacentre operators, cognisant that depreciated accelerators retain residual value principally through resale channels, have increasingly resorted to physical destruction and subsequent precious-metal recovery, thereby sterilising the secondary market entirely. This supply-side attrition insulates incumbent pricing from the deflationary pressures that historical technology cycles typically generate. For practitioners whose professional futures are entwined with infrastructure adjacent to AI deployment, the implications extend well beyond hardware acquisition costs; when generative models encroach upon functions previously requiring human judgement, the inexpensive tools that supported those workflows evaporate first.
